title: Cosmological simulations of the high-redshift galaxy population adopting a variable stellar initial mass function
comment: Main text 22 pages and 11 figures, submitted to MNRAS
summary: JWST surveys reveal a greater space density of high-redshift UV-bright galaxies than predicted by conventional galaxy formation models. We present results from a $L=100$ cMpc cosmological simulation evolved to $z=5$ with a variation of the COLIBRE galaxy formation model that adopts a density-dependent stellar initial mass function (IMF), such that stellar populations formed from dense gas are born with a top-heavy IMF. Crucially, heavy element and dust yields, and supernova feedback energetics, are self-consistently adjusted to the changing IMF. We model UV/optical emission (including nebular emission) from galaxies and its attenuation by dust. By allowing a significant fraction of high-redshift star formation to proceed with a top-heavy IMF, the rest-frame far-UV luminosities of early galaxies are elevated by up to a factor of $\simeq4$ with respect to the fiducial COLIBRE L100m6 simulation, which assumes a universal Chabrier IMF. This enables the formation of galaxies with observed brightness up to $M_{\rm UV} \simeq -20$ at $z=15$ (c.f. $M_{\rm UV} \simeq -18.5$ in the fiducial simulation), illustrating the potential of star formation with a top-heavy IMF to alleviate tensions with JWST data. Later, the boost in far-UV emission is partly offset by attenuation due to increased dust surface densities from i) additional dust grain ejection from core-collapse supernovae and ii) efficient grain growth promoted by more metal-rich interstellar gas. The simulation reproduces the $z=5$ galaxy stellar mass function and rest-frame optical luminosity function with comparable accuracy to the fiducial simulation, and both simulations exhibit UV continuum slopes that are consistent with JWST observations.

AI.tldr: A cosmological simulation with a top-heavy IMF that varies with gas density elevates far-UV luminosities of high-redshift galaxies by up to 4× compared to a universal Chabrier IMF, helping to reconcile JWST observations of overly bright z>10 galaxies with model predictions, though dust attenuation partially offsets the boost at later times.
AI.motivation: JWST surveys reveal an unexpectedly high space density of UV-bright galaxies at high redshift (z>10), which challenges conventional galaxy formation models that assume a universal IMF. This motivates exploring whether a variable, top-heavy IMF in dense star-forming regions can boost early galaxy luminosity to match observations.
AI.method: A L=100 cMpc cosmological simulation using the COLIBRE model with a density-dependent IMF (top-heavy in dense gas) is evolved to z=5. Heavy element/dust yields and supernova feedback are self-consistently adjusted. UV/optical emission including nebular emission and dust attenuation are modeled.
AI.result: Top-heavy IMF elevates rest-frame far-UV luminosities by up to ~4×, enabling M_UV ≃ -20 at z=15 vs. -18.5 in the fiducial simulation. The boost is partially offset at later times by increased dust attenuation from supernova dust ejection and grain growth. The model reproduces z=5 stellar mass function and optical luminosity function comparably to the fiducial model; both match observed UV continuum slopes.
AI.conclusion: Star formation with a top-heavy IMF can alleviate tensions between JWST observations of high-redshift UV-bright galaxies and conventional galaxy formation models, though dust attenuation becomes important at later epochs.

title: LoVoCCS. III. Third Generation Pipeline & The Hercules Supercluster
comment: Submitted to ApJS
summary: The Local Volume Complete Cluster Survey (LoVoCCS) is a volume-complete survey of over one-hundred nearby ($0.03 < z < 0.12$), X-ray luminous ($L_{500} > 10^{44} \text{ erg s}^{-1}$) galaxy clusters in the southern sky. Observations for the survey concluded in December 2025, reaching Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) Year 1-2 depth in each field and providing observations with $\lesssim 1"$ seeing for weak lensing science. In this paper, we present the latest pipeline for reducing observations using the third-generation of the LSST Science Pipelines. We use recent observations of the Hercules Supercluster to validate the pipeline's data-products and conduct an extensive multi-plane weak-lensing analysis of a $\sim 16 \text{ deg}^2$ complex covering Abell 2147, 2151, 2152, and several additional structures. We confirm that the dynamical mass of the complex is biased due to the dynamical state of Abell 2147, which is consistent with being $\sim 0.2-0.4 \text{ Gyr}$ out-of periapsis, and estimate that the total mass of the supercluster is $8.9^{+1.7}_{-1.4} \times 10^{14}~M_{\odot}$.

AI.tldr: LoVoCCS is a complete survey of ~100 nearby X-ray luminous galaxy clusters using LSST pipelines. The paper validates the reduction pipeline on the Hercules Supercluster, finding the dynamical mass of the complex is biased by Abell 2147's post-periapsis state, and estimates the supercluster total mass at 8.9 × 10¹⁴ M☉.
AI.motivation: To present and validate the latest pipeline for reducing LoVoCCS observations using LSST Science Pipelines, and to conduct weak-lensing analysis of the Hercules Supercluster complex.
AI.method: Used LSST Science Pipelines (third-generation) to reduce observations of the Hercules Supercluster, performed multi-plane weak-lensing analysis across ~16 deg² covering Abell 2147, 2151, 2152, and other structures.
AI.result: Confirmed dynamical mass bias in the complex due to Abell 2147's dynamical state (~0.2–0.4 Gyr out of periapsis); total supercluster mass estimated as 8.9⁺¹.⁷₋₁.₄ × 10¹⁴ M☉.
AI.conclusion: The LoVoCCS pipeline is validated, and the weak-lensing analysis reveals that the Hercules Supercluster's mass is significantly influenced by the dynamical state of its constituent cluster Abell 2147.

title: VAR-PZnn: A machine-learning framework for AGN photometric redshifts using color and variability-based features
comment: 18 pages, 12 figures, 4 tables, Submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics Journal
summary: Photometric redshift estimation for active galactic nuclei (AGNs) remains a fundamental challenge for current and upcoming large-scale photometric surveys. Traditional spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting suffers from color-redshift degeneracies, particularly for AGNs whose power-law continua hide the strong spectral features required to anchor redshift estimates. While AGN variability provides additional constraining power, existing frameworks require multi-band light curves that are not always available. This work presents VAR-PZnn, a fully connected mixture density network that integrates 26 variability features extracted from ZTF g-band light curves with optical photometry from Pan-STARRS1, mid-infrared (MIR) photometry from CatWISE, and, for a subsample, NIR photometry from UKIDSS. The model is trained and tested on 72,728 spectroscopically confirmed AGNs/QSOs spanning 0.01 < z < 4.5 and g-band magnitudes from 17 to 21.5. For the main sample, we achieve σ_{NMAD} = 0.058 and an outlier fraction of η= 8.2%, which reduces to 5.4% when the 10% of sources with the highest predicted uncertainty are excluded. An ablation study demonstrates that MIR photometry provides the dominant constraint for photo-z accuracy, while variability features serve as a secondary refiner. Using UKIDSS NIR data as a proxy for future synergies between LSST and space-based missions like Euclid and Roman, we obtain η= 13.3% without MIR data and η= 4.6% when MIR is available. We benchmark against Low-Resolution Templates (LRT) SED fitting (η= 28.7%) and the VAR-PZ framework; applying single-band VAR-PZ priors worsens LRT performance to η= 39.4% due to single-band light-curve degeneracies, confirmed via simulations (η= 27.6% to 28.1%). This framework provides a scalable approach for the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST).

AI.tldr: VAR-PZnn, a mixture density network combining 26 variability features from ZTF g-band light curves with multi-band photometry (Pan-STARRS1, CatWISE, UKIDSS), achieves σ_NMAD=0.058 and outlier fraction η=8.2% for AGN photometric redshift estimation across 0.01<z<4.5, significantly outperforming traditional SED fitting (η=28.7%). MIR photometry provides the dominant constraint while variability features serve as secondary refiners.
AI.motivation: Photometric redshift estimation for AGNs is fundamentally challenging due to color-redshift degeneracies from power-law continua that hide strong spectral features. Existing methods either rely on SED fitting that suffers from these degeneracies or require multi-band light curves that are often unavailable.
AI.method: A fully connected mixture density network (VAR-PZnn) integrating 26 variability features from ZTF g-band light curves with optical (Pan-STARRS1), MIR (CatWISE), and NIR (UKIDSS) photometry, trained on 72,728 spectroscopically confirmed AGNs/QSOs.
AI.result: σ_NMAD=0.058, η=8.2% (5.4% after excluding 10% highest-uncertainty sources); ablation study shows MIR photometry dominates accuracy while variability features refine; outperforms LRT SED fitting (η=28.7%); single-band VAR-PZ priors worsen LRT to η=39.4%.
AI.conclusion: VAR-PZnn provides a scalable, accurate approach for AGN photo-z estimation, particularly promising for LSST and future synergies with Euclid/Roman, where NIR+MIR combination yields η=4.6%.

title: The size of the HI disk across different environments: isolated, compact groups, clusters, and pairs
comment: 21 pages, 8 figures. Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics. Analysis code and data: https://github.com/ianjarog/galaxydisksize ; online material: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21415323
summary: The 21 cm line of atomic hydrogen (HI) is a sensitive tracer of the outer disk of galaxies, where environmental signatures are most apparent. The relative extent of HI disks compared to optical disks ($D_{\rm HI}$ vs $D_{25}$) is thought to provide a quantitative measure of such imprint, yet systematic comparisons between extreme environments remain scarce. We quantify the relative extent of HI disks in Hickson Compact Groups (HCGs) and in the Analysis of the interstellar Medium in Isolated GAlaxies (AMIGA) sample, using AMIGA as a control sample that captures secular evolution with minimal external influence. We calculate HI diameters by directly fitting an ellipse to the $1\,M_{\odot}\,{\rm pc}^{-2}$ iso-density contour. Because $D_{\rm HI}$ and $D_{25}$ are nonlinearly related, we avoid the traditional $D_{\rm HI}/D_{25}$ ratio, which carries a size-dependent bias, and instead quantify truncation as the residual from the isolated-galaxy $D_{\rm HI}$-$D_{25}$ baseline, which we establish for AMIGA via Bayesian analysis. The full analysis is provided as a reproducible Python package and Snakemake workflow. HCG galaxies lie systematically below the isolated-galaxy baseline in the $D_{\rm HI}$-$D_{25}$ plane. When members with HI nondetections are included as upper limits, HCGs have HI disks at least ~71% smaller than expected for isolated galaxies of the same optical diameter. The truncation increases monotonically along the HCG evolutionary sequence, from Phase 1 to Phase 3. A comparison with literature samples places HCGs at the most-truncated end, statistically indistinguishable from the Virgo cluster sample (VIVA). Compared to AMIGA, HI disks are typically smaller relative to the optical disk in loose groups, compact groups, and cluster infall/field environments, and are most strongly truncated in HCGs and in the Virgo cluster sample.

AI.tldr: HI disks in Hickson Compact Groups are at least ~71% smaller than expected for isolated galaxies, with truncation increasing along the HCG evolutionary sequence, and HCGs being among the most truncated environments comparable to the Virgo cluster.
AI.motivation: To quantify how environmental processes truncate HI disks in compact groups compared to isolated galaxies, using AMIGA as a control sample to establish a baseline free from environmental influences, and to systematically compare truncation across different environments.
AI.method: HI diameters measured by fitting ellipses to the 1 M⊙ pc⁻² iso-density contour; avoided the biased D_HI/D_25 ratio; established isolated-galaxy D_HI-D_25 baseline via Bayesian analysis on AMIGA; quantified truncation as residual from this baseline; used reproducible Python/Snakemake workflow; included HI nondetections as upper limits.
AI.result: HCGs lie systematically below the isolated-galaxy baseline; HI disks at least ~71% smaller than expected; truncation increases monotonically from Phase 1 to Phase 3 along the HCG evolutionary sequence; HCGs are statistically indistinguishable from Virgo cluster (VIVA) and are at the most-truncated end compared to literature samples.
AI.conclusion: HI disks are typically smaller relative to optical disks in denser environments (loose groups, compact groups, cluster infall/field) and are most strongly truncated in HCGs and the Virgo cluster, demonstrating that environmental processes significantly suppress HI extent.

title: Superorbital variability in the quiescent black hole X-ray transient A0620-00
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: Quiescent black hole low-mass X-ray binaries provide a key setting for probing accretion physics at low luminosities. A0620-00, the archetypal system in this class, has remained in X-ray quiescence for decades and exhibits complex optical variability, yet the long-term behaviour of its accretion flow remains poorly understood. Here, we report an analysis of long-term optical monitoring of A0620-00 from ZTF, LCO, and ATLAS. The full dataset spans nearly two decades, with the ZTF light curve providing the primary $\sim 2760$-day baseline for the period analysis. We identify a superorbital cycle with a period of $P = 261.9 \pm 9.4$ d and a peak-to-peak amplitude of $\sim 0.2$ mag. The signal is recovered independently across all three surveys, and red-noise simulations indicate that it is unlikely to arise from stochastic variability alone. Furthermore, the relative occurrence of the \textit{passive} and \textit{active} quiescent states displayed by the system seems to depend on the superorbital phase, with passive states concentrated near the cycle minimum and active states more common near maximum. We find that, among the possible interpretations, retrograde nodal precession of a hot inner accretion flow might be able to explain the observed long-term modulation. In this interpretation, the periodic signal may arise from cyclic reorientation of the inner flow, which modulates the photometric contribution from the innermost regions. The inferred modulation period would correspond to a characteristic dynamical radius of $\sim0.13a$ ($\sim10^4~R_{\rm g}$), where $a$ is the binary semi-major axis, broadly consistent with the expected transition between the outer thin disc and the inner hot accretion flow.

AI.tldr: Analysis of ~2760 days of optical monitoring of A0620-00 reveals a 261.9-day superorbital cycle (~0.2 mag amplitude) detected across ZTF, LCO, and ATLAS surveys. The quiescent state (passive vs. active) correlates with superorbital phase. The modulation is likely due to retrograde nodal precession of a hot inner accretion flow at ~0.13a (~10⁴ Rg).
AI.motivation: To understand long-term accretion flow behavior in quiescent black hole low-mass X-ray binaries at low luminosities, using A0620-00 as an archetypal case.
AI.method: Long-term optical monitoring from ZTF (primary, ~2760-day baseline), LCO, and ATLAS spanning nearly two decades. Period analysis, red-noise simulations, and correlation of quiescent state classification with superorbital phase.
AI.result: A 261.9 ± 9.4 d superorbital period with ~0.2 mag amplitude, independently confirmed across three surveys, unlikely from stochastic red noise. Passive quiescent states cluster near cycle minimum, active states near maximum.
AI.conclusion: Retrograde nodal precession of a hot inner accretion flow can explain the modulation, corresponding to a dynamical radius of ~0.13a (~10⁴ Rg), consistent with the outer thin disc to inner hot flow transition region.

title: Fragmentation of massive clumps: constant mass fraction and growing mass inequality of cores
comment: 11 pages, 9 figures, accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: The fragmentation of massive molecular clumps into dense cores sets the initial conditions for stellar clusters, yet how core mass distributions evolve remains unclear. Using the ALMAGAL survey (1,013 clumps and 6,348 cores), we analyze the Gini coefficient of core mass distributions for the 514 clumps containing at least four cores ($N_{\rm frag} \ge 4$), which host 5,728 cores in total. We find that the most massive core consistently accounts for $\sim 38\%$ of the total core mass ($f_{\rm core,max} \approx 0.38$), with no systematic trend with the total mass of the core per clump $M_{\rm core,tot}$. The Gini coefficient increases with total core mass ($M_{\rm core,tot}$, $r=0.55$) and evolutionary stage ($L/M$, $r=0.38$). Clumps with $L/M > 6.0$ have significantly higher Gini values (median $0.62$) than those with $L/M \le 6.0$ (median $0.49$; $p = 4.23\times10^{-15}$). These results demonstrate that while the mass fraction of the most massive core is constant, overall mass inequality among cores grows systematically as clumps evolve.

AI.tldr: Using ALMAGAL survey data (1,013 clumps, 6,348 cores), the study finds that the most massive core in a clump consistently holds ~38% of total core mass regardless of clump properties, but the Gini coefficient of core mass distributions increases with total core mass and evolutionary stage (L/M), indicating growing mass inequality as clumps evolve.
AI.motivation: To understand how the fragmentation of massive molecular clumps into dense cores sets initial conditions for stellar clusters, specifically how core mass distributions evolve over time, which remains unclear.
AI.method: Analyzed Gini coefficients of core mass distributions from 514 clumps (with ≥4 cores, total 5,728 cores) in the ALMAGAL survey, examining correlations with total core mass (M_core,tot) and evolutionary stage (L/M).
AI.result: Most massive core fraction is constant at ~38% with no trend vs. total core mass. Gini coefficient positively correlates with M_core,tot (r=0.55) and L/M (r=0.38). Clumps with L/M>6.0 show significantly higher Gini (median 0.62) than those with L/M≤6.0 (median 0.49, p=4.23×10⁻¹⁵).
AI.conclusion: While the mass fraction of the most massive core remains constant, overall mass inequality among cores systematically increases as clumps evolve, revealing key evolutionary behavior in core mass distributions.

title: Detectability of Gravitational-wave counterparts of EP-FXTs observed during the O4b LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Observing Run
comment: Submitted. Comments are welcome
summary: Fast X-ray transients (FXTs) detected by the Einstein Probe mission have emerged as a rapidly growing class of extragalactic transients, whose physical origin remains uncertain. Compact binary coalescence (CBC) systems have been proposed as one possible progenitor for at least a subset of these events, making FXTs promising targets for multi-messenger studies with gravitational-wave (GW) observations. This work presents the first systematic investigation of GW counterparts to FXTs observed by Einstein Probe and assesses the detectability of associated CBC. We focus on FXTs detected during the second half of the fourth observing run (O4b) of the Advanced LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA detector network by searching for temporal coincidences with GW candidates from the fifth Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog (GWTC-5). We analyze a sample of 47 FXTs, including 11 with measured redshifts, and assess the significance of the association between FXTs and GW candidates using a ranking statistic. We find no significant GW counterpart associated with any FXT in our sample. In the absence of a detection, we place 90% exclusion-distance constraints under the assumptions of binary neutron star and neutron star-black hole progenitor scenarios. For observations with the full LIGO and Virgo detector network, the typical median exclusion distances are $\sim$178 Mpc and $\sim$349 Mpc, respectively. These constraints disfavor a nearby compact-binary merger origin. Longer periods of joint observations by the LVK and Einstein Probe, combined with improved GW detector sensitivity, will enhance the prospects for identifying genuine GW-FXT associations and place tighter constraints on the progenitor scenarios of these events.

AI.tldr: This study presents the first systematic search for gravitational-wave (GW) counterparts to 47 FXTs detected by Einstein Probe during LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA's O4b run. No significant associations were found, leading to 90% exclusion-distance constraints (~178 Mpc for BNS, ~349 Mpc for NSBH) that disfavor nearby compact-binary merger origins for these FXTs.
AI.motivation: Fast X-ray transients (FXTs) detected by Einstein Probe are a rapidly growing class of extragalactic transients with uncertain physical origins. Compact binary coalescence (CBC) systems have been proposed as potential progenitors, making FXTs promising targets for multi-messenger studies with gravitational-wave observations. This work aims to systematically test this association for the first time.
AI.method: The authors search for temporal coincidences between 47 FXTs (11 with measured redshifts) detected by Einstein Probe during O4b and GW candidates from GWTC-5. They assess the significance of associations using a ranking statistic and, in the absence of detections, derive 90% exclusion-distance constraints for binary neutron star (BNS) and neutron star-black hole (NSBH) progenitor scenarios.
AI.result: No significant GW counterpart was found for any FXT in the sample. Under BNS and NSBH progenitor assumptions, the typical median exclusion distances with the full LIGO-Virgo network are ~178 Mpc and ~349 Mpc, respectively.
AI.conclusion: The constraints disfavor a nearby compact-binary merger origin for the observed FXTs. Future joint observations with improved GW detector sensitivity and longer baselines are needed to identify genuine GW-FXT associations and better constrain progenitor models.

title: Tidal Structures Around Edge-On Galaxies in Deep Imaging Surveys
comment: 45 pages, 13 figures, accepted for publication in MDPI Galaxies
summary: We present a statistical study of low-surface-brightness (LSB) tidal structures in two large samples of edge-on disk galaxies. Our primary sample comprises 5606 galaxies from the Edge-on Galaxies In SDSS (EGIS) catalog, analyzed using imaging from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys, supplemented by Hyper Suprime-Cam Subaru Strategic Program (HSC-SSP) data and deep Apache Point Observatory (APO) follow-up observations for selected objects. To assess the robustness of our results, we also examine an independent sample of 14,237 galaxies from the Edge-on Galaxies in the Pan-STARRS survey (EGIPS) catalog. All images were processed using a homogeneous procedure optimized for the detection of faint diffuse emission. Tidal structures were identified through visual inspection and classified into established morphological categories, with careful treatment of imaging artifacts and galactic cirrus contamination. We detected tidal features in 324 EGIS galaxies and 690 EGIPS galaxies, corresponding to incidence rates of 5.8% and 4.8%, respectively. Restricting the analysis to completeness-limited subsamples yields consistent fractions of 6.4% and 6.2%. At a typical DESI $r$-band surface-brightness depth of 28.6 mag arcsec$^{-2}$ these values are consistent with previous observational studies but lower than predictions from many cosmological simulations. Recent high-resolution simulations, however, produce incidence rates much closer to those measured here, suggesting that numerical resolution, realistic modeling of observational and instrumental effects, and galaxy formation physics are all critical for accurately predicting the abundance of LSB tidal structures.

AI.tldr: Statistical study of low-surface-brightness tidal structures in ~20,000 edge-on disk galaxies from SDSS/Pan-STARRS, finding detection rates of 4.8-6.4%, consistent with observations but lower than most simulations.
AI.motivation: To quantify the incidence of low-surface-brightness tidal structures in edge-on disk galaxies and reconcile discrepancies between observational rates and cosmological simulation predictions.
AI.method: Two large samples: EGIS (5,606 galaxies) and EGIPS (14,237 galaxies). Homogeneous image processing optimized for faint diffuse emission detection, visual inspection and morphological classification, with careful artifact/cirrus handling. Completeness-limited subsamples for consistency.
AI.result: Tidal features detected in 324 EGIS (5.8%) and 690 EGIPS (4.8%) galaxies. Completeness-limited subsamples yield 6.4% and 6.2%. Consistent with previous observations but lower than most cosmological simulations.
AI.conclusion: Recent high-resolution simulations better match observed incidence rates. Numerical resolution, realistic observational/instrumental effects, and galaxy formation physics are critical for accurate predictions of LSB tidal structure abundance.

title: Simultaneous radio, optical and X-ray monitoring of hard X-ray selected AGN: a variability study
comment: 13 pages plus Appendix, 5 figures, 3 tables. Accepted in A&A
summary: AGN emission is intrinsically variable across the electromagnetic spectrum. Mapping the coupling between the accretion disk, the X-ray corona, and ejection flows is key to understanding the energy flow within the central engine. We characterize the multi-wavelength variability of 14 hard X-ray selected AGN from the INTEGRAL/IBIS catalog in the radio, optical, and X-ray bands, to determine the coupling between these frequencies and how variability relates to the physical properties of the central engine, with emphasis on the radio band. We analyzed multi-epoch observations from AMI-LA at 15 GHz, ZTF in the g and r bands, and Swift/XRT over 2018--2020. Variability was quantified using the normalized excess variance, the fractional variability amplitude, and the Mexican Hat filter at 70- and 200-day timescales. We also characterized the radio-loudness of the sample and evaluated the impact of variability on the Fundamental Plane of black hole activity by comparing time-averaged with strictly simultaneous data. Significant variability is detected in 86% of the sample, with a clear amplitude stratification: the fractional rms amplitude is highest in X-rays, with a median of 30% (11-67%), followed by the optical g and r bands at 19% (2-33%) and 8.5% (0.2-24%), and the radio band at 10% (4-23%). The Mexican Hat analysis reveals a red-noise power spectrum dominated by long-term fluctuations. The sample follows the expected Fundamental Plane scaling; although individual sources shift within the relation due to stochastic fluctuations, this dispersion accounts for only ~3% of the total scatter. Our findings support a core-dominated origin for the 15 GHz emission, likely a compact jet base or a magnetized corona, while differences in variability patterns, radio-loudness, and Fundamental Plane location point toward distinct accretion/ejection processes and degrees of corona-jet coupling.

AI.tldr: This study characterizes multi-wavelength variability of 14 hard X-ray selected AGN from INTEGRAL/IBIS catalog using radio (AMI-LA 15 GHz), optical (ZTF g/r bands), and X-ray (Swift/XRT) data over 2018-2020. Variability is highest in X-rays (median 30%), followed by optical (19% g, 8.5% r) and radio (10%). The sample follows the Fundamental Plane scaling with only ~3% additional scatter from stochastic fluctuations. Results suggest core-dominated 15 GHz emission from a compact jet base or magnetized corona, with variability patterns indicating distinct accretion/ejection processes.
AI.motivation: To understand the energy flow within AGN central engines by mapping the coupling between the accretion disk, X-ray corona, and ejection flows through multi-wavelength variability analysis.
AI.method: Multi-epoch observations from AMI-LA (15 GHz), ZTF (g, r bands), and Swift/XRT were analyzed over 2018-2020. Variability was quantified using normalized excess variance, fractional variability amplitude, and Mexican Hat filter at 70- and 200-day timescales. Radio-loudness characterization and Fundamental Plane analysis using both time-averaged and strictly simultaneous data were performed.
AI.result: 86% of the sample shows significant variability. Fractional rms amplitude stratification: X-rays 30% (11-67%), optical g 19% (2-33%), optical r 8.5% (0.2-24%), radio 10% (4-23%). Red-noise power spectrum dominated by long-term fluctuations. Sample follows Fundamental Plane scaling with ~3% additional scatter from stochastic variability.
AI.conclusion: The 15 GHz emission likely originates from a compact jet base or magnetized corona (core-dominated). Differences in variability patterns, radio-loudness, and Fundamental Plane positions suggest distinct accretion/ejection processes and varying degrees of corona-jet coupling across the sample.

title: Asymmetries in spatially unresolved 21-cm emission line profiles of isolated galaxies
comment: Accepted for publication in MNRAS. The catalog will be available as supplementary material with the online version of the paper at MNRAS
summary: The origin of asymmetry in the ${\rm H}\,{\scriptsize{\rm I}}$ of galaxies remains an elusive problem, largely due to the difficulties associated with distinguishing between its secular and external contributors. We have compiled a sample of local isolated galaxies from the UNAM-KIAS and the latest AMIGA samples with near-complete beam coverage and robust estimates of ${\rm H}\,{\scriptsize{\rm I}}$ line asymmetry. The ${\rm H}\,{\scriptsize{\rm I}}$ measurements are based on single-dish spectra sourced from five surveys: ${\rm H}\,{\scriptsize{\rm I}}$-MaNGA, NIBLES, KLUN, ALFALFA, and xGASS. Our galaxies tend to be late-type, star-forming centrals at all masses but exhibit slightly lower specific star formation rates (sSFRs) and higher ${\rm H}\,{\scriptsize{\rm I}}$ contents than expected. The latter is likely driven by lower star formation efficiency, weaker outflows, and additionally, higher accretion rate of gas onto the galaxy at $M_\star\lesssim 10^{10.3}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$. AMIGA, however, shows systematically higher ${\rm H}\,{\scriptsize{\rm I}}$ masses than UNAM-KIAS, which we attribute to higher local densities probed by the latter. Furthermore, both samples show bar frequencies similar to normal spirals, indicating that the gravitational instabilities leading to bars predominantly stem from internal processes, as suggested by recent works. Our galaxies show unexpectedly high merger fractions, possibly due to sampling bias and/or the inability of the classification method to distinguish between flybys and encounters leading to coalescence. We also find higher sSFRs for asymmetric galaxies below $M_\star\sim 10^{10.3}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$, in agreement with the predictions for centrals from the ${\scriptsize{\rm EAGLE}}$ simulation. We release the ${\rm H}\,{\scriptsize{\rm I}}$ measurements along with ancillary galaxy and halo properties for public use.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes H I asymmetry in isolated galaxies using data from UNAM-KIAS and AMIGA samples, finding that asymmetric galaxies have higher specific star formation rates at lower masses, bar frequencies similar to normal spirals, and unexpectedly high merger fractions, with H I measurements publicly released.
AI.motivation: The origin of H I asymmetry in galaxies is poorly understood due to difficulty distinguishing secular (internal) from external (interaction/merger) mechanisms.
AI.method: Compiled local isolated galaxies from UNAM-KIAS and AMIGA samples with near-complete beam coverage; used H I single-dish spectra from five surveys (H I-MaNGA, NIBLES, KLUN, ALFALFA, xGASS); measured H I line asymmetry and compared galaxy properties.
AI.result: Galaxies show lower sSFRs and higher H I content than expected; AMIGA has higher H I masses than UNAM-KIAS due to local density differences; bar frequencies similar to normal spirals; unexpectedly high merger fractions; asymmetric galaxies below ~10^10.3 M☉ show higher sSFRs, consistent with EAGLE simulations.
AI.conclusion: Asymmetry at lower masses is linked to higher gas accretion and star formation; bars arise from internal instabilities; merger fractions may be inflated by sampling bias or flyby misclassification; H I measurements and ancillary data are released publicly.

title: A Four-Dimensional Gaussian Random Field Generator for Modeling Spatiotemporal Variability in Astrophysical Sources
comment: 10 pages, 3 figures
summary: Semi-analytic models of black-hole movies require both an emitting flow prescription and a time-dependent source variability. Existing prescriptions are often limited to either equatorial emission or time-independent sources. In this work we present a unified model for these two ingredients. First, we prescribe an off-equatorial, nongeodesic Kerr fluid rotation law by lifting an equatorial specific-angular-momentum profile to cylindrical surfaces, setting the polar component of the four-velocity to zero, normalizing the flow with the full Kerr metric at the spacetime point, and retaining the option to recover a geodesic-like plunging prescription when needed. Second, we use this velocity as the disk advection field in a four-dimensional inhomogeneous, anisotropic Matérn-like Gaussian random field. We provide a parametrized model for a torus-like disk and a central jet through a single composite correlation tensor. The resulting effective model is an implementation-ready prescription for time-dependent thick-disk and disk-jet emission for relativistic studies.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a unified semi-analytic model for black-hole movies that combines off-equatorial, nongeodesic Kerr fluid rotation with a time-dependent Matérn-like Gaussian random field to produce realistic thick-disk and disk-jet emission prescriptions for relativistic studies.
AI.motivation: Existing semi-analytic models for black-hole movies are limited to either equatorial emission or time-independent sources, lacking a unified framework that incorporates both off-equatorial flow and time-dependent variability.
AI.method: The model (1) prescribes off-equatorial nongeodesic Kerr fluid rotation by lifting an equatorial specific-angular-momentum profile to cylindrical surfaces, setting the polar four-velocity to zero, normalizing with the full Kerr metric, and optionally recovering geodesic-like plunging; (2) uses this velocity as the advection field in a 4D inhomogeneous, anisotropic Matérn-like Gaussian random field; (3) constructs a composite correlation tensor for torus-like disk and central jet emission.
AI.result: An implementation-ready prescription for time-dependent thick-disk and disk-jet emission for relativistic studies.
AI.conclusion: The unified model provides a practical, parametrized framework for generating realistic time-varying black-hole movies with both disk and jet components.

title: Molecule-dependent Abundance Behavior of Oxygen-bearing Complex Organics in High-Mass Star-Forming Regions: A Uniform 50-source Survey
comment: 9 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables, accepted for publication in A&A
summary: We present a uniform IRAM-30\,m survey analysis of four oxygen-bearing complex organic molecules (COMs), methanol (CH$_3$OH), acetaldehyde (CH$_3$CHO), methyl formate (CH$_3$OCHO), and dimethyl ether (CH$_3$OCH$_3$), toward 50 high-mass star-forming regions (HMSFRs) associated with 6.7\,GHz methanol masers. Column densities were derived through a homogeneous rotation-diagram approach, with CH$_3$CN used as a proxy excitation-temperature reference when needed. In CH$_3$OH-normalized abundance-ratio space, CH$_3$OCHO/CH$_3$OH and CH$_3$OCH$_3$/CH$_3$OH show the strongest pairwise correlation, whereas the correlations involving CH$_3$CHO are weaker. No clear monotonic trends are found with Galactocentric distance or beam-averaged H$_2$ column density. Comparison with previous observations places the CH$_3$OCHO--CH$_3$OCH$_3$ behavior within the range of earlier abundance-ratio measurements, while CH$_3$CHO shows larger inter-study variation. A representative warm-up chemical model is used only for qualitative comparison with the observed abundance ranges, which are most closely matched during the decline from the post-desorption abundance peaks in the model. These results provide homogeneous beam-averaged abundance-ratio constraints for common O-bearing COMs in high-mass star-forming regions and show that their source-to-source behavior is molecule-dependent rather than fully described by a single common abundance pattern.

AI.tldr: A homogeneous IRAM-30m survey of four O-bearing complex organic molecules (CH3OH, CH3CHO, CH3OCHO, CH3OCH3) toward 50 high-mass star-forming regions shows molecule-dependent abundance-ratio variations, with CH3OCHO and CH3OCH3 strongly correlated, no clear Galactic trends, and qualitative agreement with warm-up chemical models near post-desorption decline phases.
AI.motivation: To systematically constrain the abundance patterns and chemical behavior of common oxygen-bearing complex organic molecules in high-mass star-forming regions using a large, homogeneous data set to understand whether a single common abundance pattern applies.
AI.method: IRAM-30m survey of 50 HMSFRs associated with 6.7 GHz methanol masers; homogeneous rotation-diagram analysis for column densities with CH3CN as excitation temperature proxy; CH3OH-normalized abundance-ratio correlation analysis; comparison with warm-up chemical models.
AI.result: CH3OCHO/CH3OH and CH3OCH3/CH3OH show strongest pairwise correlation; CH3CHO correlations are weaker; no clear trends with Galactocentric distance or H2 column density; CH3OCHO–CH3OCH3 ratios consistent with prior work; CH3CHO shows larger inter-study variation; observed ranges best matched by model post-desorption decline phase.
AI.conclusion: Source-to-source abundance-ratio behavior is molecule-dependent, not fully described by a single common abundance pattern; homogeneous constraints are provided for O-bearing COMs in high-mass star-forming regions.

title: Fermi-LAT Detection of a Gamma-ray Excess toward the Radio-quiet Narrow-line Seyfert 1 Galaxy 1H 1934-063
summary: We report a $γ$-ray excess toward the radio-quiet narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxy 1H 1934-063 using data collected by the Large Area Telescope (LAT) on board the Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope and taking into account the LAT 16-year Source List (FL16Y). During the flare interval, the excess is detected in the 1--500 GeV band at a significance of $\sim 5.2σ$ (TS = 27.12), with a photon flux of $(4.94\pm2.33)\times10^{-10}$ ph cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$ and a hard photon index of $Γ=1.50\pm0.25$. The best-fit $γ$-ray position is consistent with the radio position of 1H 1934-063, while the nearby source FL16Y J1936.9-0552 is not significantly detected during the same interval. In the absence of contemporaneous multiwavelength data, the broadband interpretation cannot be tightly constrained. A compact nonthermal component can produce the hard GeV emission, but the present data do not allow a unique physical interpretation. The excess therefore provides an interesting case for probing high-energy activity in radio-quiet NLS1 galaxies, although the underlying physical mechanism remains uncertain.

AI.tldr: A γ-ray excess is detected toward the radio-quiet NLS1 galaxy 1H 1934-063 during a flare, with ~5.2σ significance, hard spectrum (Γ=1.50), and positional consistency with the radio source, but the physical origin remains ambiguous without multiwavelength data.
AI.motivation: To investigate high-energy (γ-ray) activity in a radio-quiet narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxy, a class not typically associated with such emission, using Fermi-LAT data from the FL16Y catalog.
AI.method: Analysis of Fermi-LAT data in the 1–500 GeV band during a flare interval, using the LAT 16-year Source List (FL16Y), with positional cross-matching and significance testing via Test Statistic (TS).
AI.result: Detection at ~5.2σ (TS=27.12), photon flux (4.94±2.33)×10⁻¹⁰ ph cm⁻² s⁻¹, hard photon index Γ=1.50±0.25; the γ-ray position aligns with the radio position of 1H 1934-063, while the nearby FL16Y J1936.9-0552 is not significantly detected in the same interval.
AI.conclusion: The γ-ray excess provides an interesting case for probing high-energy activity in radio-quiet NLS1 galaxies, but the underlying physical mechanism remains uncertain due to the absence of contemporaneous multiwavelength data.

title: Predicting the unpredictable: binary--single scattering with machine learning
comment: 10 pages, 5 figures
summary: Binary--single encounters occur frequently in stellar systems, constitute a non-integrable chaotic three-body problem, and are computationally expensive when treated with N-body codes. We aim to construct an accurate and physically interpretable surrogate model for binary--single scattering final states (ionization, flyby, exchange, or hierarchical), evaluate the reliability of its probabilistic predictions, and trace its predictive failures to the underlying chaotic nature of the scattering problem. We trained an XGBoost multiclass classifier on a class-balanced dataset of numerically integrated binary--single scattering experiments, using physically motivated features. The model achieves a test accuracy of 88.32 percent and a top-2 accuracy of 98.77 percent. Feature importance indicates binary hardness as the dominant predictor. Misclassifications concentrate near the chaotic boundary separating exchange and hierarchical outcomes. Basin-entropy analysis reveals that such misclassifications are due to intrinsically ambiguous regions of parameter space. Therefore, a fast machine-learning surrogate can predict binary--single scattering final states with high accuracy, and residual errors arise from chaotic regions rather than model inadequacy.

AI.tldr: The paper develops an XGBoost-based surrogate model to predict outcomes of binary-single star encounters (ionization, flyby, exchange, hierarchical), achieving 88.32% accuracy; misclassifications are concentrated near chaotic boundaries and explained by intrinsic parameter-space ambiguity rather than model inadequacy.
AI.motivation: Binary-single encounters are computationally expensive to simulate with N-body codes and constitute a non-integrable chaotic three-body problem; the authors seek a fast, interpretable surrogate to replace expensive integrations.
AI.method: An XGBoost multiclass classifier was trained on a class-balanced dataset of numerically integrated binary-single scattering experiments using physically motivated features. Basin-entropy analysis was used to quantify chaotic boundaries and explain misclassifications.
AI.result: Test accuracy of 88.32% and top-2 accuracy of 98.77%; binary hardness is the dominant feature. Misclassifications concentrate near the chaotic exchange/hierarchical boundary.
AI.conclusion: A fast ML surrogate can accurately predict binary-single scattering final states, and residual errors stem from intrinsically chaotic regions of parameter space rather than model limitations.

title: Electromagnetic Emission from a Black Hole Evaporating in External Magnetic Field
comment: 22 pages, 3 figures
summary:
We describe a classical (non-quantum) radiation process: additional (to Hawking) emission by a black hole evaporating in an external magnetic field in vacuum. The electromagnetic radiation process is completely electric charge-free and bears some resemblance to the Gertsenshtein-Zel'dovich effect. The time evolution of the spacetime metric perturbs a static background magnetic field, inducing a radiative field that acts as an effective electromagnetic source even in the absence of physical charges or currents. To isolate the dynamic effects of the time-dependent spacetime on the external magnetic field, we approximate Hawking radiation as a spherically symmetric outflow of null fluid governed by the prescribed time-dependence of the central mass $M(t)$.
  We employ Laplace transform, which selects the retarded outgoing branch of the electromagnetic response, producing fields proportional to $Θ(t-r)$ and thereby fixing a causal radiative arrow of emission. The emitted spectral energy is red-dominated, scaling as $d\mathcal{E}_B/dω\propto B_0^2 m_0^2 τ_H^{-2/3} ω^{-8/3}$, where $τ_H$ is the Hawking evaporation timescale, and corresponds to a pure Transverse Electric (TE) mode. There is no final bright burst at the end of the evaporation. We offer classical analogues for this mechanism as transmission-line emission and, separately, as the displacement current emission from a medium with time-varying dielectric permittivity.

AI.tldr: This paper describes a classical electromagnetic radiation process from a black hole evaporating in an external magnetic field, independent of Hawking radiation, producing red-dominated TE-mode emission without a final burst, analogous to transmission-line or displacement current emission.
AI.motivation: To identify and characterize a classical (non-quantum) electromagnetic radiation mechanism from black holes evaporating in external magnetic fields, beyond the standard Hawking radiation.
AI.method: Hawking radiation is approximated as a spherically symmetric null fluid outflow with time-dependent central mass M(t). Laplace transform is used to select the retarded outgoing electromagnetic response branch. The background magnetic field is perturbed by the time-varying spacetime metric.
AI.result: Emitted spectral energy is red-dominated: dℰ_B/dω ∝ B₀² m₀² τ_H^{-2/3} ω^{-8/3}, corresponding to a pure Transverse Electric (TE) mode. No final bright burst occurs at the end of evaporation. The process is charge-free and resembles the Gertsenshtein-Zel'dovich effect.
AI.conclusion: The time-dependent spacetime metric perturbs a static magnetic field, inducing an effective electromagnetic source without physical charges. Classical analogues include transmission-line emission and displacement current emission from a medium with time-varying dielectric permittivity.

title: Machine learning prediction of binary formation in three-body gravitational encounters
comment: 10 pages, 6 figures
summary: Three-body encounters are frequent events in stellar systems, intrinsically chaotic, and computationally costly to model with direct N-body integration. Predicting whether such encounters lead to binary formation is therefore challenging, particularly in large-scale simulations. We aim to develop an accurate and physically interpretable machine-learning model that predicts binary formation from the initial conditions of three-body encounters, to assess its reliability, and to identify the physical parameters that most strongly determine the outcome. We trained an XGBoost binary classifier on a balanced dataset of three-body scattering experiments computed with the REBOUND code and the IAS15 integrator. The input to the model consists of 30 physically motivated features describing the masses, energies, and kinematics of the initial configuration. The classifier achieves excellent performance on a balanced test set, with accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score all above 0.94, and with ROC-AUC and PR-AUC values of 0.99. Feature-importance analysis shows that the outcome is governed primarily by the mass hierarchy and hardness ratio of the encounter, followed by velocity fraction and mass entropy. The predicted probabilities are well calibrated, with an expected calibration error (ECE) of 0.02. Inference is approximately 400 times faster than direct N-body integration. The model also generalizes well across encounter radii, although its performance decreases in the weak-interaction regime where binary formation becomes intrinsically rare. These results show that machine learning can provide fast, accurate, and physically interpretable predictions of binary formation in three-body encounters. Such models offer a practical complement to direct N-body simulations and may enable efficient probability estimates in large-scale simulations of stellar systems.

AI.tldr: The paper presents an XGBoost binary classifier that predicts binary formation in three-body stellar encounters using 30 physically motivated features. The model achieves >0.94 accuracy/F1, ROC-AUC of 0.99, runs ~400x faster than direct N-body integration, and identifies mass hierarchy and hardness ratio as key predictors.
AI.motivation: Three-body encounters are frequent, chaotic, and computationally expensive to model with direct N-body integration, making binary formation prediction challenging, especially in large-scale simulations.
AI.method: Trained an XGBoost binary classifier on a balanced dataset of three-body scattering experiments using REBOUND/IAS15. Input: 30 physically motivated features (masses, energies, kinematics). Feature importance analyzed via calibrated probability outputs (ECE=0.02).
AI.result: Accuracy, precision, recall, F1 >0.94; ROC-AUC=0.99; PR-AUC=0.99; ECE=0.02; ~400x faster than N-body integration. Key features: mass hierarchy > hardness ratio > velocity fraction > mass entropy. Generalizes well across encounter radii but degrades in weak-interaction regime.
AI.conclusion: Machine learning provides fast, accurate, and physically interpretable predictions of binary formation in three-body encounters, serving as a practical complement to direct N-body simulations for large-scale stellar systems.

title: Optically Thick Outflow Driven by Supercritical Accretion May Explain Little Red Dots
comment: Accepted for publication in ApJL
summary: Recent JWST observations have revealed a population of compact, optically red sources known as Little Red Dots (LRDs). A popular interpretation is that LRDs host massive black holes embedded in dense gaseous envelopes, yet the physical origin of such envelopes remains unclear. We propose that the optically thick outflow driven by supercritical accretion onto black holes may explain the envelope. Based on an analytic radiative hydrodynamic outflow model, we relate the outflow properties to the black hole mass $M$ and dimensionless accretion rate $\dot{m}$. With $M\sim10^5-10^7\,M_\odot$ and $\dot m \sim 1500-5000$, the outflow photosphere reaches luminosities of $10^{43}-10^{45}\,\rm erg\,s^{-1}$ and temperatures of $\sim 3000-6000$ K, effectively matching the red optical continua observed in LRDs. The presence of a thick scattering region beyond the photosphere is central to deciphering the distinctive properties of LRDs. For each object, if one derives $M$ and $\dot{m}$ from the observed luminosity and temperature, while accounting for both kinematic broadening and scattering effects, the model predicts an emission line FWHM consistent with observations within a factor of 1.5 for more than 80\% objects. Furthermore, with Cloudy simulations, we find that the partially ionized gas beyond the photosphere produces Balmer breaks broadly consistent with measurements.

AI.tldr: LRDs may be explained by supercritical accretion onto black holes driving optically thick outflows, with model predictions matching observed luminosities, temperatures, emission line widths, and Balmer breaks.
AI.motivation: JWST has revealed Little Red Dots (LRDs), but the physical origin of the dense gaseous envelopes around their putative massive black holes remains unclear.
AI.method: Analytic radiative hydrodynamic outflow model for supercritical accretion, combined with Cloudy simulations for the ionization structure.
AI.result: The model reproduces observed LRD luminosities (10^43-10^45 erg/s) and temperatures (3000-6000 K) for M~10^5-10^7 M_sun and dot(m)~1500-5000. For >80% of objects, predicted FWHM matches observations within a factor of 1.5. Balmer breaks are also broadly consistent.
AI.conclusion: Supercritical accretion-driven outflows are a viable explanation for the compact, red optical continua and line properties of LRDs, with a thick scattering region beyond the photosphere being key to their distinctive features.

title: Temporal Correlations Between Fuzzy Dark Matter and Baryonic Matter in Virialized Core-Halo Structures
comment: 11 pages, 10 figures, accepted for publication in Phys. Rev. D
summary: Fuzzy Dark Matter (FDM) predicts the existence of virialized halos with interference-driven granular structure generated by the wave nature of ultralight bosons. Since these fluctuations produce time-dependent gravitational fields, they can be proposed as a potential source of observable dynamical effects on baryonic matter. In this work we test whether such fluctuations generate measurable temporal correlations between FDM and a coupled gas component. We evolve coupled FDM-gas configurations with the Schrödinger-Poisson-Euler system in three dimensions. The FDM component is initialized through multimerger configurations that relax toward core-halo structures, while the baryonic component is modeled as an ideal gas. After virialization, we analyze the temporal fluctuations of both components through correlation functions and spectral diagnostics. The FDM density field shows fluctuations with significant high-frequency content, whereas the gas develops smoother and longer-lived coherent structures. Although the gas dynamically responds to the gravitational potential generated by the FDM halo, we find no strong temporal correlation between the interference-driven fluctuations of FDM and the gas dynamics. This behavior persists across the explored range of gas temperatures. Our results indicate that baryonic matter reacts to the global gravitational potential of the virialized halo rather than to the detailed phase-dependent granular structure of FDM. This weak temporal coupling may limit the possibility of directly detecting FDM granularity through local baryonic temporal fluctuations.

AI.tldr: This paper tests whether interference-driven granular fluctuations in Fuzzy Dark Matter halos produce measurable temporal correlations with coupled baryonic gas dynamics. Using 3D Schrödinger-Poisson-Euler simulations of virialized FDM-gas systems, the authors find that while gas responds to the global gravitational potential of the FDM halo, there is no strong temporal correlation between the granular FDM fluctuations and gas behavior, suggesting that direct detection of FDM granularity via local baryonic temporal fluctuations may be limited.
AI.motivation: To test whether the time-dependent gravitational fields generated by interference-driven granular structure in Fuzzy Dark Matter halos can produce measurable dynamical effects on baryonic matter, potentially enabling direct detection of FDM granularity.
AI.method: Coupled 3D simulations of the Schrödinger-Poisson-Euler system: FDM initialized via multimerger configurations relaxing to core-halo structures, baryonic gas modeled as an ideal gas. After virialization, temporal fluctuations of both components are analyzed using correlation functions and spectral diagnostics across a range of gas temperatures.
AI.result: FDM density fields exhibit significant high-frequency fluctuations; gas develops smoother, longer-lived coherent structures. No strong temporal correlation is found between FDM interference-driven fluctuations and gas dynamics across all explored gas temperatures.
AI.conclusion: Baryonic matter responds primarily to the global gravitational potential of the virialized FDM halo rather than to phase-dependent granular structure, limiting the feasibility of detecting FDM granularity through local baryonic temporal fluctuations.

title: Optical observations on the young Type Ia SN 2021fxy with detached high velocity features
comment: 19 pages, 9 figures, accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: We present optical observations on the young type Ia supernova (SN Ia) SN 2021fxy obtained within a few days after the explosion, with a focus on its prominent high-velocity features (HVFs). It reached a $B$-band maximum of $M_{\rm max}(B) = -19.36\pm0.31$ mag, corresponding to a bolometric luminosity of $\sim 1.3\times10^{43}~\rm{erg~s^{-1}}$ with a synthesized $^{56}$Ni mass of $0.58\pm0.14$ M$_{\odot}$. The early spectra exhibit strong HVFs of intermediate-mass elements that are significantly detached from the photospheric components. In particular, the velocity of the Si II $\lambda6355$ HVFs follows a power-law evolution ($β\approx 0.1$), shallower than the expected photospheric velocity evolution expected for an assumed $n=10$ density profile ($β\approx 0.22$) under homologous expansion. This behavior is consistent with the HVFs forming in intrinsic ejecta structures at least partially decoupled from the bulk outer ejecta, providing a possible constraint on the explosion physics of SNe Ia.

AI.tldr: This paper presents early optical observations of SN 2021fxy, a young type Ia supernova, focusing on its high-velocity features (HVFs). The HVFs of intermediate-mass elements show a shallower velocity evolution than expected, suggesting they form in intrinsic ejecta structures partially decoupled from the bulk outer ejecta.
AI.motivation: To study the early-phase optical observations of SN 2021fxy, particularly its prominent high-velocity features (HVFs), and to understand their origin and implications for the explosion physics of Type Ia supernovae.
AI.method: Optical observations of SN 2021fxy were conducted within days after explosion. Light curve and spectral analysis were performed, including measuring HVF velocities of Si II λ6355 and comparing their power-law evolution (β ≈ 0.1) with the expected photospheric velocity evolution under homologous expansion (β ≈ 0.22 for n=10 density profile).
AI.result: SN 2021fxy reached M_max(B) = -19.36±0.31 mag, bolometric luminosity ~1.3×10^43 erg/s, with 0.58±0.14 M⊙ of ^56Ni. The Si II λ6355 HVFs show a power-law evolution with β≈0.1, shallower than the expected β≈0.22 for an n=10 density profile.
AI.conclusion: The shallow velocity evolution of HVFs supports the scenario that HVFs form in intrinsic ejecta structures at least partially decoupled from the bulk outer ejecta, providing constraints on the explosion physics of SNe Ia.

title: Disentangling the Morphology of Palomar~5: Effects of the Bar, Spiral Arms, LMC, and Halo Flattening
comment: 27 pages, 10 figures, 11 tables; accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal (ApJ) on 16 July 2026
summary: The Palomar~5 (Pal~5) globular cluster and its tidal tails provide a sensitive probe of globular-cluster evolution in the time-dependent Milky Way potential. We study the past 3~Gyr evolution of Pal~5 using collisional direct \(N\)-body simulations with \texttt{PeTar}, adopting Galactic potential models that include spiral arms, the Galactic bar, halo flattening, the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC), and bar deceleration. We find that halo shape strongly influences the projected stream track, reflecting Pal~5's sensitivity to Galactic force-field flattening. The LMC causes only modest direct changes to the present-day projected stream morphology, but can alter the pericentric distance and hence the progenitor's mass evolution. The Galactic bar strongly affects stream length and debris redistribution along the tails, producing model-dependent density structures and leading--trailing asymmetries. Comparison with observations from Erkal et al. (2017) and Xiao et al. (2025) shows that no single model simultaneously reproduces all observed properties of Pal~5, including cluster evolution, stream length, track, width, and line-density profile. Although our simulations capture several global properties, the remaining discrepancies indicate that a more precise match likely requires better constraints on the initial properties of the Pal~5 progenitor and a more complex Galactic potential, including perturbations from small-scale perturbers such as dark matter subhalos and giant molecular clouds. Future work may combine self-consistent direct \(N\)-body simulations with particle-spray methods to investigate these discrepancies more efficiently.

AI.tldr: This study uses direct N-body simulations (PeTar) to model the past 3 Gyr evolution of the Palomar 5 globular cluster and its tidal tails under various Milky Way potential models (spiral arms, bar, halo flattening, LMC). Halo shape strongly affects the stream track, the bar influences stream length and density asymmetries, and the LMC alters pericentric distance and mass loss. No single model fully matches all observed properties, suggesting need for better progenitor constraints and inclusion of small-scale perturbers.
AI.motivation: Palomar 5 and its tidal tails serve as a sensitive probe of globular cluster evolution in a time-dependent Galactic potential, motivating a detailed investigation of how various components of the Milky Way (spiral arms, bar, halo flattening, LMC, bar deceleration) affect its evolution and stream morphology.
AI.method: Collisional direct N-body simulations using the PeTar code, incorporating Galactic potential models with spiral arms, Galactic bar, halo flattening, LMC, and bar deceleration, run over a 3 Gyr timespan.
AI.result: Halo shape strongly influences the projected stream track; LMC has modest direct effects on morphology but alters pericentric distance and mass evolution; Galactic bar drives stream length changes and trailing-leading density asymmetries. No single model simultaneously reproduces cluster evolution, stream length, track, width, and line-density profile when compared to observations (Erkal+2017, Xiao+2025).
AI.conclusion: Better constraints on the Pal~5 progenitor's initial properties and inclusion of small-scale perturbers (dark matter subhalos, giant molecular clouds) are needed. Future work should combine direct N-body simulations with particle-spray methods for more efficient investigation.

title: Beyond Spin: QCD Magnetars
comment: 37 journal pages, 2 figures, 9 tables and 6 appendices
summary: We present a unified framework in which anomalous X-ray pulsars (AXPs), soft gamma-ray repeaters (SGRs), superluminous supernovae (SLSNe-I), luminous fast blue optical transients (LFBOTs), and fast radio bursts (FRBs) originate from quark deconfinement in the core of a massive neutron star (NS). Spontaneous ferromagnetism in the deconfined phase generates ~10^18 G core fields, producing a highly magnetized hybrid star (HS) - the "QCD magnetar" - whose surface field is set by NS mass, not birth spin. The Quark-Nova (QN) that forms the HS ejects ~0.01M_sun of neutron-rich outer layers, powering a kilonova and leaving the HS crustless for centuries. During this phase, magnetic instabilities at the hadron-quark interface release rising flux ropes that power X-ray-quiet FRBs; as the crust reforms, the source evolves into an X-ray-loud AXP&SGR. Two parameters govern the model: a critical mass M_dec triggering deconfinement, and a critical period P_fast separating fast and slow rotators. Fast rotators inject spin-down energy into the QN ejecta, producing an LFBOT - directly observable once the SN ejecta is optically thin, or via binary accretion with no preceding SN; otherwise the LFBOT is reprocessed by the SN ejecta into an SLSN-I. A Bayesian Monte Carlo population synthesis reproduces the observed rates of AXPs&SGRs, SLSNe-I, and LFBOTs with M_dec ~2.1M_sun and P_fast ~5.5 ms, and predicts non-merger r-process signatures and kilonovae from isolated NSs, with or without an LFBOT. The QN ejecta also carries its own DM and RM, independent of environment, predicted to appear as excess dispersion and rotation measure in FRBs once Galactic, host, and intergalactic contributions are removed. These provide direct observational tests of the hadron-quark phase transition and ferromagnetic ordering in dense quark matter.

AI.tldr: A unified framework proposes that AXPs, SGRs, SLSNe-I, LFBOTs, and FRBs all originate from quark deconfinement in massive neutron stars, forming highly magnetized hybrid stars ("QCD magnetars") with ~10^18 G core fields. The model predicts kilonovae, r-process signatures, and FRB dispersion/rotation measure excesses, with population synthesis matching observed rates using M_dec ~2.1 M_sun and P_fast ~5.5 ms.
AI.motivation: To unify the origins of multiple astrophysical transients (AXPs, SGRs, SLSNe-I, LFBOTs, FRBs) under a single physical mechanism — the hadron-quark phase transition in neutron star cores — rather than treating each phenomenon with separate models.
AI.method: Theoretical framework combining quark deconfinement physics, spontaneous ferromagnetism in quark matter, and Bayesian Monte Carlo population synthesis to compare predicted event rates with observations.
AI.result: Population synthesis reproduces observed rates of AXPs/SGRs, SLSNe-I, and LFBOTs with M_dec ~2.1 M_sun and P_fast ~5.5 ms. Predicts non-merger r-process signatures, kilonovae from isolated NSs, and excess dispersion/rotation measure in FRBs.
AI.conclusion: The QCD magnetar model provides testable predictions for FRB DM/RM excess and kilonovae from isolated NSs, offering direct observational tests of the hadron-quark phase transition and ferromagnetic ordering in dense quark matter.

title: Super-Jeans Fragmentation and Supply-Limited Accretion: Environment-Dependent Co-Evolution of Low- and High-Mass Cores
comment: 12 pages, 3 figures, Accepted by ApJ
summary: Protostellar core formation and growth in high-mass star-forming regions remain key to understanding massive star birth. We analyze the masses of 839 cores (resolved at scales of a few thousand au) from the ASHES project targeting 39 massive infrared dark cloud clumps. The masses of the three most massive cores scale linearly with the total core mass. They maintain a constant mass fraction of ~25%, 16%, and 10% along the mass growth sequence. These fractions reveal that the progenitor seeds destined to become high-mass cores establish their mass dominance very early. Additionally, the Gini coefficient (a statistical measure of inequality) of the core mass distributions increases along the mass growth sequence, confirming that the relative population of low-mass cores builds up toward later stages. This points to an environment-dependent fragmentation picture: central prestellar seeds rapidly evolve into high-mass cores via transport-driven super-Jeans fragmentation under rapid, non-stationary mass accumulation in high-density, turbulent hubs, subsequently maintain their dominance through supply-limited synchronized growth (at R<1 pc, n_H2>10^5 cm^-3), while the formation of the surrounding low-mass cores is relatively delayed due to their lower gas densities and the lack of non-stationary inflow acceleration effect, resulting in their continuous emergence through Jeans-like fragmentation in lower-density envelopes. This picture is consistent with a gravity-driven scenario where the local free-fall time is the controlling factor. Our analysis suggests that non-stationary density-regulated fragmentation and supply-limited accretion jointly drive the synchronized co-evolution of the core cluster, seamlessly linking small-scale core growth with large-scale reservoir regulation.

AI.tldr: Analysis of 839 cores in 39 massive IRDC clumps (ASHES project) reveals that the three most massive cores maintain constant mass fractions (~25%, 16%, 10%) along the mass growth sequence, while the Gini coefficient increases, indicating early mass dominance of high-mass cores and delayed formation of low-mass cores. This supports an environment-dependent fragmentation picture combining super-Jeans fragmentation in dense hubs and delayed Jeans-like fragmentation in lower-density envelopes, regulated by non-stationary, gravity-driven processes.
AI.motivation: To understand how protostellar cores form and grow in high-mass star-forming regions, which is key to understanding massive star birth. The study aims to uncover the evolutionary dynamics of core mass distributions and the physical mechanisms governing core cluster evolution.
AI.method: Analyzed mass distributions of 839 cores from the ASHES survey (ALMA observations of 39 massive IRDC clumps at ~few thousand au resolution). Measured mass fractions of the three most massive cores, computed Gini coefficients to quantify mass inequality, and examined evolutionary trends along the mass growth sequence.
AI.result: The three most massive cores maintain constant mass fractions (~25%, 16%, 10%) throughout the mass growth sequence. Gini coefficient increases along the sequence, indicating growing mass inequality. High-mass cores establish dominance early via super-Jeans fragmentation in dense, turbulent hubs, while low-mass cores form later via Jeans-like fragmentation in lower-density envelopes.
AI.conclusion: Core cluster evolution follows a gravity-driven, environment-dependent fragmentation picture where non-stationary density-regulated fragmentation and supply-limited accretion drive synchronized co-evolution of cores, linking small-scale core growth to large-scale reservoir regulation.

title: Time-dependent Accretion Disks in Tidal Disruption Events: Long-term Light Curves
comment: 20 pages, 13 figures; Submitted to ApJ
summary: The time-dependent accretion disk has been applied to explain the light curves observed in tidal disruption events (TDEs). Radiation pressure instability is expected to be an important factor that can shape the evolution of the accretion disk. In this paper, we upgrade the time-dependent disk model in Guo $\&$ Qiao by incorporating an index $μ$ (with the stress tensor $\propto p^μp^{1-μ}_{\rm{gas}}$, where $p=p_{\rm{gas}} + p_{\rm{rad}}$) for the modified viscosity, and a parameter $f_{\rm{w}}$ for the strength of the wind. Meanwhile, we adopt a more realistic fallback rate to inject into the disk. After systematically testing the effects of the newly incorporated parameters, we find that $f_{\rm{w}}$ can affect the time when the instability occurs, while $μ$ can influence the occurrence and variation magnitude of the radiation pressure instability. When $μ<0.4$, the radiation pressure instability is completely removed from the disk, and the light curves evolve stably without large-scale magnitude variation. When $μ>0.4$, the light curves can show oscillations caused by the instability, or drop steeply when the instability occurs and become flat in the late-time evolution, which mainly occurs when the viscous viscosity parameter $α$ is small or the impact parameter $β$ is small. Since the drop magnitude can be modulated by $μ$, we apply these `decay-to-flatten' light curves to some optical/UV observations in TDEs with different magnitudes of decline. Finally, we discuss the potential application of our model to some special TDEs that show oscillations in the light curves.

AI.tldr: This paper upgrades a time-dependent accretion disk model for TDEs by incorporating a modified viscosity index μ and wind parameter f_w. It finds that μ<0.4 suppresses radiation pressure instability entirely, while μ>0.4 can produce oscillations or decay-to-flatten light curves, which are applied to optical/UV TDE observations.
AI.motivation: To better understand how radiation pressure instability shapes TDE light curves, the authors extend previous time-dependent disk models by adding a more flexible viscosity prescription (parameterized by μ) and wind effects (f_w), along with a realistic fallback rate.
AI.method: The authors upgrade the Guo & Qiao disk model by (1) introducing a viscosity index μ where stress tensor ∝ p^μ p_gas^{1-μ}, (2) adding a wind parameter f_w, and (3) adopting a more realistic fallback rate. They systematically test how μ and f_w affect disk evolution and light curves.
AI.result: f_w affects the timing of instability onset; μ controls whether instability occurs (μ<0.4 suppresses it entirely, μ>0.4 allows oscillations or steep drops followed by flattening). The drop magnitude is modulated by μ. These decay-to-flatten light curves match optical/UV TDE observations with different decline amplitudes.
AI.conclusion: The model can reproduce diverse TDE light curve behaviors — stable evolution, oscillations, or decay-to-flatten — depending on μ, α, and β. It has potential applications to TDEs showing oscillatory light curves.

title: Ongoing Morphological Transformation from Elliptical to Spiral Galaxies Induced by Gas Accretion from Neighboring Galaxies
summary: We present results from spectroscopic observations of three interacting galaxy systems, each associated with a primary galaxy - VCC 1748, SDSS J1106, and 2MASX J0834 - which have been proposed as potential examples of reverse morphological transformation from elliptical to spiral types driven by external gas accretion. Using Gemini/GMOS longslit spectroscopy, we obtain spectra along longslits connecting the regions of interest between the two galaxies in each pair. We model the spatially binned spectra with the Penalized Pixel-Fitting (pPXF) method to derive velocity fields and radial profiles of gas-phase metallicity, stellar metallicity, and stellar population age. Among the three systems, only the VCC 1748 system provides spectra with sufficiently high signal-to-noise ratios (S/N) to reveal coherent velocity and metallicity structures extending between the companion spiral galaxy and its elliptical target. The velocity profile along the gas-bridge of the system is smooth and continuous from the companion spiral arm to the target galaxy, and the elliptical target, VCC 1748, exhibits younger stellar populations and a high star formation rate (SFR) in its newly formed disk regions compared to its central parts. These findings indicate in-situ star formation at the newly-formed spiral arm of the elliptical target, consistent with ongoing gas inflow from the spiral companion into the elliptical target. Altogether, the results capture an intermediate stage of morphological evolution in which an originally quiescent elliptical galaxy begins to assemble a rotationally supported disk through interaction-driven gas accretion.

AI.tldr: Spectroscopic analysis of three interacting galaxy systems reveals that only VCC 1748 shows clear evidence of gas inflow from a spiral companion to an elliptical galaxy, driving in-situ star formation and disk assembly, consistent with reverse morphological transformation from elliptical to spiral type.
AI.motivation: To test the hypothesis of reverse morphological transformation — where elliptical galaxies revert to spiral types via external gas accretion — by observationally examining three candidate interacting galaxy systems.
AI.method: Gemini/GMOS longslit spectroscopy combined with Penalized Pixel-Fitting (pPXF) modeling to extract spatially resolved velocity fields, gas-phase/stellar metallicity, and stellar population age profiles from the three galaxy pairs.
AI.result: Only VCC 1748 had sufficient S/N; it shows a smooth, continuous velocity profile along the gas bridge, younger stellar populations and high SFR in the disk regions of the elliptical target, indicating ongoing gas accretion and in-situ star formation.
AI.conclusion: The observations capture an intermediate stage where an elliptical galaxy begins assembling a rotationally supported disk via interaction-driven gas accretion, supporting the reverse morphological transformation scenario.

title: Black hole spin-mass correlation and vector resonant relaxation in gaseous star clusters: the origin of GW231123?
summary: During the formation of a star cluster a spin-mass correlation of stellar black holes is generated as they grow via accretion of the residual gas. Moreover, the black hole spin tends to be anti-aligned with its orbital angular momentum in the cluster. We show that GW231123, reported by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) collaboration, lies on our predicted high-mass, high-spin plateau of the spin-mass correlation with positive Bayesian evidence over the LVK prior. Furthermore, vector resonant relaxation (VRR) equilibrium is favored over the isotropic LVK prior in reproducing the distribution of the relative spin tilt. The joint Bayes factor suggests strong evidence for the favored cluster models. GW231123 is thus consistent with our proposed channel that generates correlated black hole masses and spins, and drives the spins' orientations.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that GW231123 fits a predicted spin-mass correlation from star cluster formation, with Bayesian evidence favoring cluster models over standard LVK priors, supporting a formation channel where black hole spins correlate with mass and are anti-aligned with orbital angular momentum.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that the gravitational wave event GW231123 is consistent with a predicted spin-mass correlation arising from black hole growth via gas accretion in star clusters, and to test whether vector resonant relaxation (VRR) equilibrium in clusters better explains the observed spin tilt distribution compared to isotropic priors.
AI.method: The authors compare GW231123's properties to a predicted high-mass, high-spin plateau from cluster formation models, compute Bayesian evidence against LVK priors, and evaluate the relative spin tilt distribution under VRR equilibrium versus isotropic assumptions using Bayes factors.
AI.result: GW231123 lies on the predicted high-mass, high-spin plateau with positive Bayesian evidence over the LVK prior. VRR equilibrium is favored over isotropic priors for spin tilt distribution. The joint Bayes factor shows strong evidence for the cluster models.
AI.conclusion: GW231123 is consistent with a star cluster formation channel that produces correlated black hole masses and spins with anti-aligned spin-orbit orientations, providing support for this evolutionary pathway.

title: The initial conditions and initial mass functions of Alpha Persei, Pleiades and Praesepe
comment: Accepted for publication in PASA. 27 pages, 17 figures, 7 tables
summary: We have determined the initial mass function (IMF) and structural properties of the open clusters Alpha Persei, Pleiades and Praesepe using Gaia DR3 astrometry and photometry. Cluster members were identified using primarily Gaia astrometry, supplemented with near-infrared UKIDSS and optical HIPPARCOS survey data with stellar masses down to $0.10-0.17$ MSun. We measure and correct for unresolved binaries in each cluster using photometry and Monte Carlo simulations in a Bayesian framework, finding present-day fractions between ($20.0\pm0.8$)% and ($23.8\pm1.2$)%. Through a novel approach that combines N-body simulations with machine learning emulators and MCMC algorithms, we have also determined the most probable initial number of stars, binary fraction, half-mass radius and mass function under the assumption that early gas removal does not significantly influence the subsequent cluster evolution. We find a best-fitting initial mass function described by a three-stage broken power-law distribution with break masses in the ranges $0.24-0.50$ MSun and $0.91-1.20$ MSun and average slopes of $α_{\rm med}=1.72\pm0.09$ and $α_{\rm high}=2.98\pm0.22$. While the low-mass slope remains sensitive to the adopted mass-luminosity relation, this IMF reproduces the present-day clusters well once their dynamical evolution is taken into account.
