We find evidence of scatter in the high mass IMF between the individual clusters, as described by the measured dispersions in mass function slopes of $σ_{\rm high}=0.29\pm0.16$, whereas the intermediate mass slope shows no significant variation with $σ_{\rm med}=0.00\pm0.14$. Our findings provide additional evidence for a (compared to a Salpeter MF) top-light IMF and a cluster-to-cluster variation of the IMF. They therefore provide constraints on the universality of the IMF and its dependence on environmental conditions.

AI.tldr: Using Gaia DR3 data, the study determines the IMF and structural properties of three open clusters (Alpha Persei, Pleiades, Praesepe), finding a top-light, three-stage broken power-law IMF with cluster-to-cluster variation, challenging the universality of the IMF.
AI.motivation: To constrain the universality of the initial mass function and its dependence on environmental conditions by measuring the IMF and its variation across multiple open clusters using high-precision Gaia DR3 data.
AI.method: Cluster members identified via Gaia DR3 astrometry + UKIDSS/HIPPARCOS data; unresolved binaries corrected using photometry and Bayesian Monte Carlo simulations; initial conditions inferred by combining N-body simulations with machine learning emulators and MCMC algorithms.
AI.result: Present-day binary fractions 20.0%–23.8%; best-fit IMF is a three-stage broken power-law with break masses 0.24–0.50 M☉ and 0.91–1.20 M☉, slopes α_med=1.72±0.09 and α_high=2.98±0.22; evidence of scatter in high-mass IMF (σ_high=0.29±0.16) but not intermediate-mass (σ_med=0.00±0.14).
AI.conclusion: The IMF is top-light relative to Salpeter and varies between clusters, providing evidence against a fully universal IMF and supporting environmental dependence.

title: The Complete Catalog of Gamma-Ray Transients Observed by GRBAlpha & VZLUSAT-2 CubeSat Missions
comment: submitted to The Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series, after revision
summary: We present the largest sample of gamma-ray transients observed by any CubeSat mission so far. Observations were acquired by a 1U CubeSat GRBAlpha, the smallest astrophysical space observatory, and a 3U CubeSat VZLUSAT-2. Both missions were technological pathfinders and carried a novel CsI scintillator-based detector read-out by silicon photomultipliers. They operated on Sun-synchronous low Earth orbits below 550 km for about four years; GRBAlpha between March 2021 and June 2025 while VZLUSAT-2 between January 2022 and November 2025. Despite being technological experiments, they observed over 300 gamma-ray transients including gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), solar flares, soft gamma repeaters and one outburst from an X-ray binary. Among these are the two brightest GRBs ever observed, GRB 221009A and GRB 230307A, without saturation and GRBs at redshifts up to z=4.2. GRBAlpha also contributed to the InterPlanetary Network. Regular monitoring of transients was demonstrated by a detection rate of two transients or one GRB a week and the shortest time between two subsequent detections of only 42 minutes. We show that a constellation of nanosatellites around the Earth would observe at least 60% of Fermi/GBM GRBs with 5$σ$ significance and over 90% at 3$σ$ level. GRBAlpha and VZLUSAT-2 prove that routine monitoring of the gamma-ray sky can also be done by low-cost and quickly developed nanosatellite missions.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the largest sample of gamma-ray transients observed by CubeSat missions, with GRBAlpha (1U) and VZLUSAT-2 (3U) detecting over 300 transients over ~4 years, including the brightest GRBs ever observed. The results demonstrate that low-cost nanosatellite constellations can achieve over 60% of Fermi/GBM GRB detection at 5σ significance.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that low-cost, rapidly developed nanosatellite missions can routinely monitor the gamma-ray sky, serving as technological pathfinders for future CubeSat constellations.
AI.method: Two CubeSat missions (GRBAlpha 1U, VZLUSAT-2 3U) equipped with CsI scintillator detectors read out by silicon photomultipliers, operating on Sun-synchronous LEO below 550 km from 2021–2025.
AI.result: Over 300 gamma-ray transients detected, including GRBs, solar flares, soft gamma repeaters, and an X-ray binary outburst. The two brightest GRBs ever (221009A, 230307A) were observed without saturation. Detection rate: ~2 transients or 1 GRB per week; shortest interval between detections was 42 minutes. A nanosatellite constellation could detect ≥60% of Fermi/GBM GRBs at 5σ and >90% at 3σ.
AI.conclusion: GRBAlpha and VZLUSAT-2 prove that routine gamma-ray transient monitoring is feasible with low-cost, quickly developed nanosatellite missions, paving the way for future CubeSat constellations.

title: A Rest-frame K-band View of Bulge Growth in Massive Dusty Star-forming Galaxies at z~2
comment: See Figure 4 for the key result that the stacked F770W and ALMA 870 micron profiles agree closely out to 8 kpc. Comments are welcome. Submitted to ApJ
summary: We study bulge formation in 16 massive dusty star-forming galaxies at z~2 by combining JWST MIRI F770W imaging, NIRCam imaging in eight bands, and ALMA 870 um data. At the median redshift of z=2.18, the F770W band probes the rest-frame 2.4 um light, close to the rest-frame K band, and traces the stellar mass distribution with little effect from dust attenuation. The effective radii measured in F770W agree with those of the 870 um dust emission, with a median ratio of 0.95, and are typically 23% smaller than those in F444W. The rest-frame K-band imaging is therefore essential to measure the true extent of the stellar mass, which is as compact as the dusty star-forming regions. In stacks of the 16 galaxies at a matched resolution, the 870 um and F770W profiles agree closely out to 8 kpc, and a bulge plus disk decomposition of the F770W stack gives a bulge-to-total ratio of 0.50. Fitting the SEDs in radial bins with CIGALE, we find that the attenuation decreases from Av=2.6 mag at the center to 1.5 mag at $r\gtrsim7$ kpc, while the specific star formation rate profile is flat. In these galaxies the bulge is already in place, and the whole system grows toward compact quiescent galaxies within about 1 Gyr. In two galaxies, by contrast, the 870 um emission is 3 to 6 times more compact than the F770W light, which suggests that they are still in the bulge-building compaction phase. Our sample may thus catch massive galaxies in several phases of bulge formation.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes bulge formation in 16 massive dusty star-forming galaxies at z~2 using JWST MIRI F770W, NIRCam, and ALMA 870 μm data. The rest-frame K-band (F770W) imaging reveals stellar mass distributions as compact as dusty star-forming regions, with bulge-to-total ratio of 0.50 from bulge+disk decomposition. SED fitting shows decreasing dust attenuation radially (Av 2.6→1.5 mag) and flat sSFR profiles. Most galaxies appear to be evolving toward compact quiescent galaxies within ~1 Gyr, while two galaxies show evidence of ongoing bulge-building compaction.
AI.motivation: To understand bulge formation processes in massive galaxies at cosmic noon (z~2), a key epoch when massive galaxies build their central bulges and transition from star-forming to quiescent.
AI.method: Combined JWST MIRI F770W (rest-frame ~2.4 μm), NIRCam eight-band imaging, and ALMA 870 μm continuum data. Performed radial profile comparisons, bulge+disk decomposition on stacked images, and radial SED fitting with CIGALE to measure stellar mass distributions, dust attenuation, and star formation profiles.
AI.result: F770W effective radii agree well with 870 μm radii (median ratio 0.95) but are ~23% smaller than F444W radii. Stacked profiles show close agreement between 870 μm and F770W out to 8 kpc. Bulge-to-total ratio is 0.50. Dust attenuation decreases from Av=2.6 mag (center) to 1.5 mag (r>7 kpc), while sSFR profile is flat. Two galaxies show 870 μm emission 3-6 times more compact than F770W, indicating ongoing compaction.
AI.conclusion: Rest-frame K-band imaging is essential for accurately measuring stellar mass extents in dusty z~2 galaxies. Most of these galaxies already have bulges in place and will evolve into compact quiescent galaxies within ~1 Gyr, while some are still undergoing bulge-building compaction. The sample captures multiple phases of bulge formation.

title: Quantifying the Information Gain from Future High-Precision Radius Measurements for Identifying Twin Neutron Stars
comment: 8 pages including 5 figures
summary: Twin neutron stars (NSs), characterized by identical gravitational masses but different radii, are among the most promising astrophysical signatures of a strong first-order hadron--quark phase transition in supradense matter. We investigate how increasingly precise NS radius measurements improve the Bayesian inference of twin-star observability using mock radius data for a canonical $1.4\,M_\odot$ NS. Radius uncertainties are varied from the current level of about $0.9$ km to the $\approx 0.1$ km precision anticipated from future X-ray and gravitational-wave observations. We quantify the information gained using the posterior distribution of the maximum twin-star radius separation $ΔR$ together with an analytical model of branch distinguishability and complementary information-theoretic measures based on the branch observational efficiency and the Shannon entropy. The combined analyses reveal three inference regimes: a prior-dominated regime for $σ_R \gtrsim 0.6$ km, a rapid information-gain regime for $0.2 \lesssim σ_R \lesssim 0.6$ km, and an information-saturation regime for $σ_R \lesssim 0.2$ km. These complementary analyses consistently indicate that radius measurements with a precision of about $0.2$ km already extract most of the information available for identifying twin NSs within the present Bayesian framework. Beyond establishing a quantitative observational benchmark for future high-precision radius measurements, this work provides a general Bayesian framework for quantifying the information gain from progressively more precise observations and identifying the point of diminishing scientific returns.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates how increasing precision of neutron star radius measurements (from ~0.9 km to ~0.1 km) improves Bayesian inference of twin neutron stars—objects with identical masses but different radii that signal a first-order hadron–quark phase transition. Three inference regimes are identified, with ~0.2 km precision extracting most available information.
AI.motivation: To understand how improved NS radius measurements enhance the detectability of twin stars—a key signature of a strong first-order hadron–quark phase transition—and to establish quantitative benchmarks for future high-precision observations.
AI.method: Bayesian inference using mock radius data for a 1.4 M⊙ NS with varying precision (σ_R from ~0.9 km to ~0.1 km). Information gain quantified via posterior distribution of maximum twin-star radius separation ΔR, analytical model of branch distinguishability, branch observational efficiency, and Shannon entropy.
AI.result: Three inference regimes identified: prior-dominated (σ_R ≳ 0.6 km), rapid information-gain (0.2 ≲ σ_R ≲ 0.6 km), and information-saturation (σ_R ≲ 0.2 km). Radius measurements at ~0.2 km precision capture most available information for identifying twin NSs.
AI.conclusion: A precision of ~0.2 km is the observational benchmark for twin-star identification; beyond this, diminishing returns set in. The framework generalizes to quantifying information gain from progressively precise observations.

title: Anomalously high deuterium fractionation in a galactic translucent cloud: a challenge to chemical models
comment: 7 pages, 6 figures, A&A Letters accepted
summary: Deuterated (D-) species have long been proposed to diagnose the physical conditions and chemical evolution of cold dense molecular clouds. While deuterium fractionation has been extensively measured in dense cores, observations in diffuse and translucent clouds remain rare. We report here the detection of DCN and DNC toward a translucent cloud ($A_{\rm V} =1.2\pm0.2$ mag, $n_{\rm H_2}$ = $3.9\pm0.2\times10^2$ cm$^{-3}$) through sensitive absorption observations with the IRAM NOrthern Extended Millimeter Array (NOEMA). This detection reaches the lowest column-density and volume-density regime in which deuteration has been observed so far. Interestingly, the observed DCN/HCN and DNC/HNC abundance ratios ($3.3\pm0.6\times10^{-3}$ and $3.6\pm1.2\times10^{-3}$, respectively), which are more than two orders of magnitude higher than the element abundance [D]/[H] (1.5$\times$10$^{-5}$), suggest an unexpected enhancement of deuterium fractionation in the translucent cloud. These results represent a significant departure from established chemical models considering deuterium fractionation, which predict negligible formation of D-molecules in such environments. Although it remains unclear how D-molecules built up their abundances in translucent gas, a dispersed dense core scenario could potentially explain the observed high deuterium fraction. This interpretation is consistent with the idea proposed by Price et al. (2003) more than two decades ago: a translucent cloud may be a transient, dynamically evolving structure formed through the dissipation of a dense molecular cloud.

AI.tldr: DCN and DNC are detected in a translucent cloud (AV~1.2 mag, n(H2)~390 cm⁻³), the lowest column/volume density regime where deuteration has been observed. DCN/HCN and DNC/HNC ratios (~10⁻³) exceed the elemental D/H ratio (~1.5×10⁻⁵) by >2 orders of magnitude, challenging standard chemical models. A dispersed dense core scenario or transient evolutionary structure may explain this unexpected enhancement.
AI.motivation: Deuterated species are key probes of cold, dense molecular cloud conditions, but deuterium fractionation has rarely been observed in diffuse or translucent clouds, leaving a gap in understanding chemical evolution across density regimes.
AI.method: Sensitive absorption observations of DCN and DNC toward a translucent cloud using IRAM NOEMA, measuring column densities and abundance ratios relative to HCN and HNC.
AI.result: Detection of DCN and DNC at the lowest column-density and volume-density regime ever observed; DCN/HCN = 3.3±0.6×10⁻³ and DNC/HNC = 3.6±1.2×10⁻³, more than 100× the elemental D/H ratio.
AI.conclusion: Standard deuterium fractionation models fail to predict such high deuteration in translucent gas. A dispersed dense core scenario, or the interpretation of translucent clouds as transient, evolving structures from dense cloud dissipation (Price et al. 2003), may explain the observations.

title: Two Peas in a Pod: The First Confirmed Dual Active Galactic Nucleus within a Green Pea Galaxy System
comment: 23 pages before references, 8 figures, and 2 tables. Submitted for publication
summary: The growth of galaxies in the early Universe is thought to be dominated by compact, intensely star-forming systems, yet the corresponding growth of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) within such environments remains poorly constrained. Green Pea galaxies are nearby analogs of rapidly assembling galaxies in the early Universe owing to their compact morphologies, intense star formation, low metallicities, and extreme ionization conditions. Although galaxy interactions are thought to trigger episodes of rapid SMBH growth, direct observations of simultaneous accretion onto multiple SMBHs in compact, intensely star-forming galaxies are lacking. Here we report the discovery of the first confirmed dual active galactic nucleus (AGN) in a Green Pea system, SDSS J162209.41+352107.5. Chandra imaging resolves two luminous hard X-ray sources separated by 8.4 kpc in projection, demonstrating simultaneous accretion onto two SMBHs. Follow-up Keck spectroscopy confirms that the two optical nuclei share a common redshift and independently exhibit broad Balmer emission and high-ionization AGN emission lines. Unlike most known dual AGN, which are typically found in massive mergers, J162209.41+352107.5 is a compact low-mass system analogous to galaxies thought to dominate early phases of galaxy assembly. These findings demonstrate that efficient growth of multiple SMBHs can occur in such environments and establish Green Pea galaxies as nearby laboratories for investigating the interplay between galaxy interactions, star formation, and black-hole growth under conditions analogous to those prevalent in the young Universe.

AI.tldr: This paper reports the first confirmed dual active galactic nucleus (AGN) in a Green Pea galaxy system (SDSS J162209.41+352107.5), resolved by Chandra as two hard X-ray sources separated by 8.4 kpc, with Keck spectroscopy confirming two optical nuclei sharing a common redshift and exhibiting broad Balmer and high-ionization AGN emission lines. This demonstrates that simultaneous SMBH accretion can occur in compact, low-mass, intensely star-forming environments analogous to early Universe galaxies.
AI.motivation: Observations of simultaneous supermassive black hole accretion in compact, intensely star-forming galaxies — environments analogous to early galaxy assembly — are lacking, limiting understanding of how SMBHs grow alongside their host galaxies in the early Universe.
AI.method: Chandra X-ray imaging resolved two luminous hard X-ray sources separated by 8.4 kpc; follow-up Keck spectroscopy confirmed two optical nuclei share a common redshift with broad Balmer emission and high-ionization AGN emission lines.
AI.result: Discovery of the first confirmed dual AGN in a Green Pea galaxy system (SDSS J162209.41+352107.5), showing simultaneous accretion onto two SMBHs in a compact low-mass system.
AI.conclusion: Efficient growth of multiple SMBHs can occur in compact, intensely star-forming environments, and Green Pea galaxies serve as nearby analogs to study the interplay between galaxy interactions, star formation, and black-hole growth under conditions prevalent in the young Universe.

title: The Intrinsic Multiphase Gas--Black Hole Connection across Scales in IllustrisTNG
comment: 10 pages, 5 figures, 1 table. ApJ accepted. Comments are welcome
summary: The relationship between supermassive black holes and the multiphase circumgalactic medium is central to understanding the co-evolution of galaxies and their central black holes. We investigate this relationship using the IllustrisTNG100 simulation with a sample of 5089 central galaxies at $z=0$, measuring the partial correlation between central black hole mass and the mass of cold ($T < 10^4$K), cool ($10^4 \le T < 10^5$K), warm ($10^5 \le T < 10^6$K), and hot ($T \ge 10^6$K) gas within $0.03R_{200}$, $0.15R_{200}$, and $R_{200}$, after accounting for stellar and dark matter halo mass. We find that after removing these confounding factors, black hole mass shows a significant negative partial correlation ($ρ\approx -0.37$) with cold gas within $R_{200}$ and $0.15R_{200}$, whereas warm and hot gas exhibit no substantial intrinsic correlation. The residual plane reveals a threshold pattern: galaxies with over-massive black holes show systematically reduced cold gas, consistent with the cumulative impact of AGN feedback. The anti-correlation persists across environments with a weak trend in local density, and varies with galaxy type (star-forming, green valley, and quenched). These results provide a quantitative multiphase diagnostic of AGN feedback in TNG and support a picture in which feedback progressively removes cold gas, offering testable predictions for future multiwavelength surveys.

AI.tldr: Using IllustrisTNG100 simulations, this study finds that after controlling for stellar and dark matter halo mass, supermassive black hole mass exhibits a significant negative partial correlation with cold circumgalactic gas but not with warm or hot gas, supporting AGN feedback progressively removing cold gas.
AI.motivation: To understand the co-evolution of galaxies and their central supermassive black holes by investigating the relationship between black hole mass and the multiphase circumgalactic medium (cold, cool, warm, hot gas phases) at various radii, while accounting for confounding factors like stellar and halo mass.
AI.method: Analysis of 5089 central galaxies from IllustrisTNG100 simulation at z=0; measured partial correlations between black hole mass and gas mass in four temperature phases (cold T<10^4K, cool 10^4-10^5K, warm 10^5-10^6K, hot ≥10^6K) within 0.03R_200, 0.15R_200, and R_200; controlled for stellar mass and dark matter halo mass; examined residual plane, environmental density, and galaxy type.
AI.result: Significant negative partial correlation (ρ≈-0.37) between black hole mass and cold gas within R_200 and 0.15R_200; no substantial intrinsic correlation with warm or hot gas; threshold pattern where over-massive black holes correspond to reduced cold gas; anti-correlation persists across environments with weak local density trends and varies with star-forming, green valley, and quenched galaxy types.
AI.conclusion: The results provide a quantitative multiphase diagnostic of AGN feedback in TNG simulations, supporting a picture where feedback progressively removes cold gas, and offer testable predictions for future multiwavelength surveys.

title: Revealing a multi-zone circumnuclear dust response in UGC~11487 through phase-resolved WISE W1--W2 diagnostics
comment: 20 pages, 14 figures, submited to A&A
summary: Mid-infrared (MIR) flares provide a direct probe of dust reprocessing in obscured tidal disruption event (TDE) candidates when the primary optical or ultraviolet flare is weak, missed, or strongly attenuated. We present a phase-resolved analysis of the WISE/NEOWISE W1-W2 evolution of the MIR-selected TDE candidate UGC 11487/WTP14adeqka over 2014-2024. We combine timing, colour, and flux diagnostics with phenomenological modelling, hydrodynamically motivated clumpy dust-echo calculations, and an aperture-matched ultraviolet-to-radio spectral energy distribution of the host. The decade-long flare shows a delayed and broader W2 response, colour hysteresis, and cooling from approximately 900 K to 500-600 K. Positive-fluence centroids yield a preferred delay of $224 +/- 45$ d, corresponding to $0.188 +/- 0.038$ pc. The effective infrared luminosity peaks at approximately $3 x 10^{43}$ erg s$^{-1}$, and the integrated infrared energy is $(2.9-3.8) x 10^{51}$ erg. A single self-similar MIR response is strongly disfavoured, with Delta BIC = 281.7, while the preferred compact description is a two-component phenomenological model. Representative hydro-clumpy calculations reproduce the empirical diagnostics in a structured, multi-zone dust-response scenario. The host is a moderately star-forming isolated barred disc without a dominant persistent active galactic nucleus component. These results support an obscured TDE-like accretion transient reprocessed by structured circumnuclear dust and show that phase-resolved WISE diagnostics can recover characteristic sub-parsec response scales in obscured accretion-powered nuclear transients.

AI.tldr: A decade-long (2014-2024) phase-resolved analysis of the MIR-selected TDE candidate UGC 11487/WTP14adeqka using WISE/NEOWISE data reveals dust reprocessing in an obscured tidal disruption event. Key findings include a delayed W2 response (~224 days, ~0.188 pc), color hysteresis, cooling from ~900 K to 500-600 K, peak IR luminosity ~3×10^43 erg/s, integrated energy ~(2.9-3.8)×10^51 erg, and a two-component phenomenological model favored over a single self-similar response (ΔBIC=281.7). The host is an isolated barred disc without a dominant AGN. Results support an obscured TDE-like transient reprocessed by structured circumnuclear dust.
AI.motivation: To understand dust reprocessing in obscured TDE candidates where primary optical/UV flares are weak, missed, or attenuated, by analyzing the MIR echo as a direct probe.
AI.method: Phase-resolved analysis of WISE/NEOWISE W1-W2 evolution over 2014-2024; timing, color, and flux diagnostics; phenomenological modelling; hydrodynamically motivated clumpy dust-echo calculations; aperture-matched UV-to-radio SED of the host.
AI.result: Decade-long flare with delayed/broader W2 response; color hysteresis; cooling from ~900 K to 500-600 K; delay of 224±45 d (0.188±0.038 pc); peak L_IR~3×10^43 erg/s; integrated E_IR~(2.9-3.8)×10^51 erg; two-component model strongly favored (ΔBIC=281.7).
AI.conclusion: The results support an obscured TDE-like accretion transient reprocessed by structured circumnuclear dust, demonstrating that phase-resolved WISE diagnostics can recover sub-parsec response scales in obscured accretion-powered nuclear transients.

title: On the Separation Between the Brightest Cluster Galaxy and the Intracluster Light
comment: 15 pages, 8+1 figures, submitted to ApJS. Comments are welcome!
summary: We present a model-based framework to define an aperture separation between the brightest cluster galaxy (BCG) and the intracluster light (ICL). Using the intrinsic BCG and ICL components predicted by the semi-analytic model \texttt{FEGA25}, we determine, for each halo, the aperture radius that minimizes the bias in the recovered ICL mass. The optimal radius is obtained by balancing the BCG stellar mass lying outside the aperture with the ICL mass enclosed within it. At $z=0$, the optimal aperture in physical units increases with halo mass approximately as $r_{\rm cut}\propto M_{\rm halo}^{0.28}$, close to the expected virial scaling. When expressed in units of the virial radius, the aperture becomes nearly independent of halo mass, with $r_{\rm cut}/R_{\rm vir}\simeq 0.045$ at $10^{14}M_\odot$. Applying the resulting aperture prescriptions, we recover the intrinsic BCG mass to better than 8\% (lowest percentile), while the ICL mass is recovered with median values very close to unity, and an average scatter of $\pm 3\%$. Extending the analysis to $z=1$ and $z=2$, we find that the mass trends remain similar, with the slope and intercept of $r_{\rm cut}/R_{\rm vir}$ that stay stable. Robustness tests show that the inferred aperture is most sensitive to the ICL concentration and BCG size, but the main trends are preserved. Our results provide a physically motivated aperture definition for connecting observational BCG--ICL measurements to intrinsic model components.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a model-based framework to define an optimal aperture for separating the brightest cluster galaxy (BCG) from intracluster light (ICL), minimizing bias in recovered ICL mass. The optimal aperture scales as $r_{\rm cut}\propto M_{\rm halo}^{0.28}$ and is nearly constant at $r_{\rm cut}/R_{\rm vir}\simeq 0.045$ at $z=0$. The method recovers BCG mass to better than 8% and ICL mass with median values near unity and $\pm 3\%$ scatter. Results are stable to $z=2$ and robust to variations in ICL concentration and BCG size.
AI.motivation: To provide a physically motivated, model-based definition for the aperture separation between BCG and ICL that minimizes bias in recovered ICL mass, enabling consistent comparison between observations and intrinsic model components.
AI.method: Using the semi-analytic model FEGA25 to obtain intrinsic BCG and ICL components for each halo, the optimal aperture radius is determined by balancing BCG stellar mass outside the aperture with ICL mass inside it. Scaling relations with halo mass and redshift are derived, and robustness tests against ICL concentration and BCG size are performed.
AI.result: At $z=0$, $r_{\rm cut}\propto M_{\rm halo}^{0.28}$ in physical units; in virial units $r_{\rm cut}/R_{\rm vir}\simeq 0.045$ at $10^{14}M_\odot$, nearly mass-independent. BCG mass recovered to better than 8% (lowest percentile), ICL mass recovered with median near unity and $\pm 3\%$ scatter. Trends persist at $z=1$ and $z=2$ with stable slope and intercept.
AI.conclusion: The proposed aperture definition provides a robust, physically motivated separation between BCG and ICL that is stable across mass and redshift, offering a standardized method for linking observational measurements to intrinsic model components.

title: Feature-driven anomaly flagging in obscured active galactic nucleus light curves with autoencoders
summary: Active galactic nuclei (AGN) are among the most complex classes of astrophysical objects, displaying a wide range of variability and observational properties. Identifying unusual AGN is crucial for understanding the physical mechanisms behind their emission better and for discovering potentially new subclasses or rare behaviors. With the increasing volume of data from next-generation surveys, machine-learning-based anomaly detection offers a promising approach to flagging and investigating such outliers systematically. We explore the use of unsupervised algorithms with a feature-driven approach to flag anomalous AGN, further explored by a human expert. The main focus is on obscured AGN, which tend to be harder to characterize. The algorithm we used was an AutoEncoder, which we trained on features extracted from the light curves rather than working with the light curves directly. The unsupervised nature of the method allows the detection of anomalies without relying on labeled data. To properly characterize the feature space and the detection process, we used the SHAP method. Our method flagged $11.18\%$ of the AGN we studied as anomalous. We focused in particular on anomalous obscured AGN and identified a refined subset of features that yields a comparable performance to the full set. Together with an in-depth analysis of the anomalies, this provides insight into how the AutoEncoder assigns anomalous status and which features are most indicative of astrophysically interesting behaviors or phenomena.

AI.tldr: The paper uses an unsupervised AutoEncoder trained on features extracted from light curves to detect anomalous AGN, with a focus on obscured AGN. SHAP analysis is used to interpret the feature space. The method flagged 11.18% of AGN as anomalous and identified a refined feature subset with comparable performance.
AI.motivation: Identifying unusual AGN is crucial for understanding the physical mechanisms behind their emission and discovering new subclasses or rare behaviors, especially for obscured AGN which are harder to characterize. The growing data volume from next-generation surveys necessitates automated anomaly detection.
AI.method: Unsupervised AutoEncoder trained on features extracted from light curves (rather than raw light curves), with anomaly interpretation via SHAP. Feature refinement was performed to achieve comparable performance with a reduced feature set.
AI.result: 11.18% of the studied AGN were flagged as anomalous. A refined subset of features was identified that yields comparable detection performance to the full feature set.
AI.conclusion: Unsupervised feature-driven anomaly detection with AutoEncoders, combined with SHAP interpretability, is effective for flagging anomalous AGN, particularly obscured ones, and provides insight into which features are most indicative of astrophysically interesting behaviors.

title: Far-Infrared Star Formation Rates of Quasar Host Galaxies from Multiwavelength Spectral Energy Distribution Decomposition
comment: 42 pages, 24 figures
summary: Reliable star formation rates (SFRs) are essential for studying the connection between black hole growth and quasar host galaxies. We study the far-infrared (FIR) SFRs and the host galaxy properties of 202 SDSS and PG quasars at $0.02<z\lesssim0.8$, spanning $\log({\rm SFR}_{\rm FIR}/M_\odot\,{\rm yr}^{-1})\simeq-0.45$--$2.76$, using multiwavelength spectral energy distribution (SED) decomposition. The photometry covers wavelengths from the optical to the FIR and is supplemented by JCMT/SCUBA-2 observations at 450 and 850 $μ$m. We model the SEDs with CIGALE and AGNfitter and adopt multiple cold dust templates to quantify systematic uncertainties. The median model-dependent scatter among the five FIR SFR estimates is $0.14$ dex, and AGNfitter gives FIR SFRs lower than the mean CIGALE estimate by a median of $0.09$ dex. For the 58 quasars with SCUBA-2 coverage, including SCUBA-2 data changes the adopted FIR SFR by only $\sim$0.01 dex on average but can affect individual sources with limited Herschel coverage or radio-loud emission. Within our FIR-constrained sample, many quasar hosts lie on or above the star-forming main sequence, but the redshift-dependent FIR selection of the SDSS subsample limits conclusions about the full quasar-host population. We find no clear correlation between the main-sequence (MS) offset and the direct Eddington ratio, while the offset is positively related to the infrared-based $L_{\rm tor}/L_{\rm Edd}$ proxy. The minimum radiation field intensity in the dust model, $U_{\rm min}$, increases with bolometric luminosity and dust temperature. WISE W2 (4.6 $μ$m) and W3 (12 $μ$m) combined with Herschel bands can also provide useful empirical indicators of $f_{\rm AGN}$.

AI.tldr: Study of FIR SFRs and host galaxy properties for 202 quasars (z<0.8) using multiwavelength SED decomposition with CIGALE and AGNfitter, supplemented by JCMT/SCUBA-2 observations. Finds median model-dependent scatter of 0.14 dex in FIR SFR, no clear correlation between MS offset and Eddington ratio, but positive relation with L_tor/L_Edd proxy.
AI.motivation: Reliable SFRs are essential for studying the connection between black hole growth and quasar host galaxies.
AI.method: Multiwavelength SED decomposition using CIGALE and AGNfitter with multiple cold dust templates, supplemented by JCMT/SCUBA-2 450 and 850 μm observations for 58 quasars.
AI.result: Median model-dependent scatter in FIR SFRs is 0.14 dex; AGNfitter gives ~0.09 dex lower values. SCUBA-2 data changes FIR SFR by ~0.01 dex on average. Many hosts lie on/above star-forming MS. No clear correlation between MS offset and Eddington ratio, but positive correlation with L_tor/L_Edd. U_min increases with bolometric luminosity and dust temperature.
AI.conclusion: FIR SFR estimates show systematic model dependencies. SCUBA-2 has minimal average impact but matters for individual sources. Redshift-dependent FIR selection limits full population conclusions. WISE W2+W3 with Herschel bands provide useful f_AGN empirical indicators.

title: The stability of radially anisotropic rotating stellar systems with a central density cusp
comment: 12 pages and 14 figures. Submitted, comments welcome
summary:
We investigate the interplay between radial velocity anisotropy and internal rotation in self-gravitating systems characterised by initial spherical symmetry and a moderate density cusp. We study the stability properties of such configurations to disentangle the impact of anisotropy, rotation, and density structure on the formation of triaxial stellar systems.
  We perform a set of collisionless $N$-body simulations starting from initial equilibria with a phase space distribution function of the class introduced by Osipkov and Merritt, modified to impose a net global angular momentum with the Lynden-Bell daemon protocol. We analyse the growth of the density and phase space distribution modes, as well as the axial ratios and triaxiality index of the final configurations. We find that internal rotation has a mitigating effect on the strength of the radial orbit instability in radially anisotropic models with Fridman-Polyachenko-Shukhman index close to its value for consistency, while it slightly enhances the onset of the instability in nearly stable models. From the analysis of the growth rate of the density modes, we also find that an inner bar, though unstable for maximally rotating initial conditions, is formed even in systems with initial profiles with a central density cusp.

AI.tldr: This study uses N-body simulations to examine how radial velocity anisotropy and internal rotation interact in self-gravitating systems with initial spherical symmetry and a moderate density cusp, finding that rotation mitigates radial orbit instability in radially anisotropic models but slightly enhances it in nearly stable models, and that inner bars can form even in cuspy systems.
AI.motivation: To disentangle the impact of anisotropy, rotation, and density structure on the formation of triaxial stellar systems, and to understand the stability properties of such configurations.
AI.method: Collisionless N-body simulations starting from Osipkov-Merritt initial equilibria with net angular momentum imposed via the Lynden-Bell daemon protocol; analysis of density/phase space distribution modes, axial ratios, and triaxiality index.
AI.result: Internal rotation mitigates radial orbit instability in radially anisotropic models with Fridman-Polyachenko-Shukhman index near its consistency value, but slightly enhances instability in nearly stable models; an inner bar forms even in cuspy systems under maximally rotating initial conditions.
AI.conclusion: Rotation and anisotropy interact in a nuanced way in determining the stability and shape evolution of self-gravitating systems, with rotation acting as a stabilizing factor for strongly anisotropic models and a destabilizing one for marginally stable configurations.

title: Structural and dynamical properties of Tidal dwarf galaxies in the tails and bridge of the Guitar galaxy Arp 105
summary: We present a multi-wavelength (far-ultraviolet to infrared) analysis of two tidal dwarf galaxy (TDG) candidates and a tidal bridge in the interacting system Arp 105 at $z = 0.029$ in the Abell 1185 cluster. Far-ultraviolet observations obtained with the Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope onboard AstroSat reveal strong FUV emission from the tidal galaxies Arp~105N and Arp~105S, indicating recent star formation. In Arp~105N, strong nebular emission lines and large equivalent widths $EW(Hα)=77.6\pm1.3$ $\overset{\circ}{\mathrm {A}}$ and $EW(Hβ)=15.8\pm1.7$ $\overset{\circ}{\mathrm {A}}$ imply a dominant starburst age of $\sim$6 - 10~Myr under an instantaneous-burst assumption, while the FUV emission suggests star formation sustained over the past $\sim100 - 200$~Myr. The relatively high metallicity, $\sim2/3,Z_\odot$ (based on the strong-line method), is consistent with expectations for a tidal dwarf galaxy formed from material inherited from the host galaxy. Together, these results suggest that Arp~105N hosts a composite stellar population, consisting of older stars stripped from the host galaxy and younger stars formed in situ. Spectral energy distribution modeling yields stellar masses of $5.75\times10^{9}$, $0.8\times10^{9}$, and $6.8\times10^{9},\rm M_\odot$ for Arp~105N, Arp~105S, and the tidal bridge, respectively. Based on the dynamical mass estimate from VLA HI measurements for Arp~105N and based on CFHT H$α$ kinematics for A105S, they have a dynamical-to-baryonic mass ratio of $\sim1.95$ and $\sim1.30$, respectively, indicating a deficiency of dark matter. Further observations, particularly integral field spectroscopy and high-resolution 21~cm observations, may provide better constraints into the kinematics and improve understanding of TDG formation.

AI.tldr: Multi-wavelength (FUV-to-IR) analysis of Arp 105 interacting system reveals two tidal dwarf galaxy candidates (Arp~105N and Arp~105S) and a tidal bridge, with Arp~105N showing recent starburst activity (~6-10 Myr), sustained star formation over ~100-200 Myr, high metallicity (~2/3 Z☉), composite stellar population, stellar masses of 5.75×10⁹, 0.8×10⁹, and 6.8×10⁹ M☉, and dynamical-to-baryonic mass ratios of ~1.95 and ~1.30 indicating dark matter deficiency.
AI.motivation: To study the star formation activity, stellar populations, metallicity, and dark matter content of tidal dwarf galaxy candidates in the interacting system Arp 105, probing the formation and evolution of TDGs in a cluster environment.
AI.method: Multi-wavelength analysis using AstroSat/UVIT FUV data, optical spectroscopy (Hα, Hβ equivalent widths), strong-line metallicity diagnostics, SED fitting for stellar masses, and dynamical mass estimates from VLA HI and CFHT Hα kinematics.
AI.result: Arp~105N shows starburst age ~6-10 Myr, sustained SF over ~100-200 Myr, metallicity ~2/3 Z☉, composite stellar population (stripped old + in-situ young stars). Stellar masses: 5.75×10⁹ (N), 0.8×10⁹ (S), 6.8×10⁹ M☉ (bridge). Dynamical-to-baryonic mass ratios ~1.95 (N) and ~1.30 (S), indicating dark matter deficiency.
AI.conclusion: Arp~105N hosts a composite stellar population with ongoing star formation and near-solar metallicity consistent with TDG origin from host material. Both TDG candidates show dark matter deficiency. Further IFU and high-resolution 21 cm observations are needed for better kinematic constraints.

title: Testing [O II] $\lambda3727$ as a Star Formation Rate Tracer in Quasar Host Galaxies
comment: 25 pages, 8 figures
summary: The [O II] $\lambda3727$ emission line is a widely used star formation rate (SFR) tracer. However, its application to type I quasars is not straightforward, because the line can be affected by dust extinction, metallicity and contamination from the AGN narrow-line region (NLR). We test the reliability of [O II] SFRs using a sample of 202 SDSS and PG quasars, by comparing [O II] SFRs and reference far-infrared (FIR) SFRs derived from multiwavelength SED decomposition. We measure [O II], [O III], and narrow Balmer emission lines by spectral fitting. Then, we calculate [O II] SFRs after correcting dust extinction and metallicity. We then compare these SFRs with the FIR SFRs, both with and without subtracting the AGN contribution estimated from [O III]. After this correction, the median offset between [O II] and FIR SFRs is $-0.20\pm0.72$ dex for the full analysis sample and $-0.17\pm0.69$ dex for sources with S/N $>5$ in both [O II] and [O III]. Without subtracting the AGN contribution, the corresponding offsets are $0.00\pm0.69$ and $0.12\pm0.66$ dex. We conclude that [O II] is useful as a statistical SFR tracer for quasar host galaxies, but individual objects still require careful treatment of AGN contamination, extinction, metallicity, aperture effects, and redshift-dependent systematics.

AI.tldr: This study tests the reliability of [O II] λ3727 emission as a star formation rate (SFR) tracer for type I quasars by comparing [O II]-derived SFRs with reference far-infrared (FIR) SFRs from SED decomposition in a sample of 202 SDSS and PG quasars. After correcting for dust extinction, metallicity, and AGN contamination (via [O III]), the median offset is -0.20±0.72 dex, indicating [O II] is useful as a statistical SFR tracer but requires careful individual treatment.
AI.motivation: [O II] λ3727 is widely used as an SFR tracer, but its application to type I quasars is complicated by dust extinction, metallicity, and AGN narrow-line region contamination. This study aims to test its reliability for quasar host galaxies.
AI.method: Using 202 SDSS and PG quasars, the authors measured [O II], [O III], and narrow Balmer lines via spectral fitting. They calculated [O II] SFRs after correcting for dust extinction and metallicity, then compared them with FIR SFRs from multiwavelength SED decomposition, both with and without subtracting the AGN contribution estimated from [O III].
AI.result: With AGN contribution subtracted, the median offset between [O II] and FIR SFRs is -0.20±0.72 dex for the full sample and -0.17±0.69 dex for high-S/N sources. Without AGN subtraction, offsets are 0.00±0.69 and 0.12±0.66 dex, respectively.
AI.conclusion: [O II] is useful as a statistical SFR tracer for quasar host galaxies, but individual objects require careful treatment of AGN contamination, extinction, metallicity, aperture effects, and redshift-dependent systematics.

title: Spatio-kinematical structure of the Galactic Nuclear Stellar Disk revealed in VLBI astrometry of circumstellar masers
comment: 11 pages, 4 figures, Published in Advancing Astrophysics with SKA II (AASKAII), 2026 (arXiv:2606.20366). Report-no:AASKAII/Imai01
summary: SKA-VLBI astrometry will enable us to measure up to thousands of three dimensional motions of OH masers associated with circumstellar envelopes (CSEs) of OH/IR stars in the Nuclear Stellar Disk (NSD) and sites of high mass star formation in the Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) of the Galactic Center (GC). It is expected that the spatio-kinematical distribution of those OH masers should indicate the existence of a ring structure in the NSD, which has formed as a result of outward propagation of star-formation activities in the GC. This is likely visualized clearly by a group of OH/IR stars, some of which should have stellar pulsation periods of >400 days and the corresponding ages of <500 Myr, and some sites of ongoing star formation. These OH/IR stars should host 1612-MHz OH masers, some of which should become targets of huge-sample VLBI astrometry, in moderate accuracy, in SKA-MID Band 2 (~1.6 GHz). The data of maser source proper motions will exhibit a stream motion in the stellar ring structure. Furthermore, the information of accurate distances (error <100 pc) of the maser sources are necessary to directly find the major-axis direction of a possible elliptical ring of stars at ~8 kpc. These distances may be yielded through trigonometric parallaxes measurable in SKA-MID Band 5a (5--7 GHz) and/or photometric parallaxes derived from the pulsation period--luminosity relation of long period variable stars hosting the maser sources.

AI.tldr: This paper discusses how SKA-VLBI astrometry can measure 3D motions of OH masers in the Galactic Center's Nuclear Stellar Disk and Central Molecular Zone, enabling detection of a ring structure through proper motions and parallax measurements.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that SKA-VLBI astrometry can map the spatio-kinematical distribution of OH masers in the Galactic Center, revealing a stellar ring structure formed by outward propagation of star formation activities in the NSD and CMZ.
AI.method: Using SKA-MID Band 2 (~1.6 GHz) for VLBI astrometry of 1612-MHz OH masers to measure proper motions, and SKA-MID Band 5a (5-7 GHz) for trigonometric parallaxes, complemented by photometric parallaxes from the period-luminosity relation of long period variable stars.
AI.result: The proper motion data will show stream motions in the stellar ring structure; distances with <100 pc accuracy can be obtained via trigonometric or photometric parallaxes to determine the major-axis direction of an elliptical ring at ~8 kpc.
AI.conclusion: SKA-VLBI astrometry of OH masers is a powerful tool to probe the three-dimensional structure and kinematics of the Galactic Center, particularly the NSD ring and CMZ star formation regions.

title: Ergodicity of FIRE: star formation variations within and between simulated galaxies
comment: 17 pages, 11 figures, 2 tables. Published in ApJ
summary: We investigate the ergodicity of star formation in simulated galaxies from the FIRE-2 (Feedback In Realistic Environments) project. We restrict ergodicity considerations to being related to deviations from the star-forming main sequence (SFMS), and in turn whether ensemble averages across populations match time-averaged star formation histories (SFHs) based on simulated observable properties. We find that in these high-resolution simulations the deviations of individual galaxies from the SFMS tend to approach ergodic behavior over time, regardless of the SFMS definition adopted and the star formation estimator used. This trend persists when galaxy morphology, as traced by Sérsic index, is considered despite the spheroid-dominated morphologies showing a smaller range of SFMS deviations than the disk-dominated morphologies. Unsurprisingly, we find more rapid convergence to ergodic behavior for star formation estimators based on shorter time scales ($10^{7}$ years) as opposed to longer ($10^{9}$ years). We caution that these findings should be considered in the context of the current sample and that further studies, particularly of high redshift evolution and the impact of active galactic nuclei should be investigated.

AI.tldr: Using FIRE-2 simulations, the authors find that individual galaxies' deviations from the star-forming main sequence tend toward ergodic behavior over time, meaning ensemble averages across galaxies approximate time-averaged star formation histories of individual galaxies.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether star formation in galaxies is ergodic — i.e., whether averaging across a population of galaxies at a given time yields the same result as time-averaging the star formation history of individual galaxies — which has implications for interpreting observed galaxy populations.
AI.method: Analyzed high-resolution cosmological simulations from the FIRE-2 project, comparing ensemble averages of galaxy star formation rates (deviations from the SFMS) to time-averaged individual star formation histories, tested across different SFMS definitions, star formation estimators (10^7 vs 10^9 yr timescales), and galaxy morphologies (Sérsic index).
AI.result: Individual galaxies' SFMS deviations approach ergodic behavior over time regardless of SFMS definition or estimator used; shorter-timescale estimators converge more rapidly; spheroid-dominated morphologies show smaller ranges of SFMS deviations than disk-dominated ones.
AI.conclusion: Ergodicity of star formation holds in FIRE-2 simulations, but caution is warranted regarding sample size; further studies on high-redshift evolution and AGN feedback are needed.

title: Comparing the Near-infrared Spectral Energy Distributions from Different Stellar Population Synthesis Models with SPHEREx Observations
comment: Submitted to ApJ, 24 pages, 10 figures, 3 appendices
summary: While stellar population synthesis (SPS) models have been widely used for spectral analysis in optical wavelengths, their characteristics remain uncertain in the near-infrared (NIR) due to a relative lack of observed NIR spectra. The spectrophotometric data from SPHEREx are well-suited for investigating the performance of SPS models in the NIR, thanks to its wide wavelength coverage over $0.7-5.0~{\rm μm}$. In this work, we compare the observed SPHEREx data of SDSS compact galaxies, including 2,726 non-emission-line galaxies and 1,163 emission-line galaxies, to the NIR SEDs predicted from the full spectrum fitting of SDSS optical spectra. We use four different SPS models that extend into the NIR: E-MILES, Bruzual \& Charlot (BC03), Charlot \& Bruzual (CB19), and FSPS. We find that all four models tend to overpredict the stellar continuum at $2.4-5~{\rm μm}$ by $0.1-0.3~{\rm mag}$. This trend is particularly prominent for intermediate-age stellar populations ($\sim1-5~{\rm Gyr}$), suggesting a systematic bias in the NIR SED predictions of current SPS models. For stellar populations older than $5~{\rm Gyr}$, E-MILES shows relatively smaller offsets at $3.8-5~{\rm μm}$ compared to other models. Meanwhile, for emission-line galaxies, the SPS models underestimate the SED by up to $\sim0.5~{\rm mag}$ at longer wavelengths due to the contribution of non-stellar emission. Overall, these results highlight the necessity of refining the NIR stellar spectral features in SPS models, such as emissions from thermally pulsating asymptotic giant branch stars or molecular absorptions from cool stars.

AI.tldr: This study uses SPHEREx spectrophotometric data (0.7–5.0 μm) for 3,889 SDSS compact galaxies to test four SPS models (E-MILES, BC03, CB19, FSPS) in the NIR. All models overpredict the 2.4–5 μm stellar continuum by 0.1–0.3 mag, especially for intermediate-age populations (1–5 Gyr). E-MILES performs better for >5 Gyr populations at 3.8–5 μm. For emission-line galaxies, models underestimate the SED by ~0.5 mag due to non-stellar emission, highlighting the need to refine NIR stellar features like TP-AGB stars and molecular absorptions.
AI.motivation: The NIR characteristics of SPS models remain uncertain due to a lack of observed NIR spectra; SPHEREx provides a unique opportunity to evaluate model performance in this underexplored wavelength regime.
AI.method: Compared SPHEREx NIR photometry (0.7–5.0 μm) of 2,726 non-emission-line and 1,163 emission-line SDSS compact galaxies against NIR SEDs predicted from full-spectrum fitting of SDSS optical spectra using four SPS models (E-MILES, BC03, CB19, FSPS).
AI.result: All models overpredict NIR continuum at 2.4–5 μm by 0.1–0.3 mag, most prominent for 1–5 Gyr populations. E-MILES has smaller offsets at 3.8–5 μm for >5 Gyr populations. Emission-line galaxies show underestimation by ~0.5 mag at longer wavelengths due to non-stellar emission.
AI.conclusion: Current SPS models have systematic biases in NIR predictions; refinements to NIR stellar spectral features—particularly TP-AGB stars and cool-star molecular absorptions—are necessary.

title: The science of the cycle of matter in our Galaxy with the SKA
comment: Published in Advancing Astrophysics with the SKA II (AASKAII), 2026(arXiv:2606.20366). Report-no: AASKAII/Audard01
summary: Exploring how matter cycles through the Galaxy, from the birth of stars in dense interstellar clouds to the ejection of matter and energy during a star's final stages-requires a multi-faceted approach. Radio observations are essential to reveal the intricate interactions at play. By studying our Galaxy in detail, we can use it as a model to better understand these processes in galaxies as well. The Square Kilometre Array offers unique capabilities in wide-field, high-sensitivity, high-resolution spectroscopy and precise astrometry to revolutionise Galactic astrophysics. This chapter presents an overview of the science addressed in detail in chapters pertinent to the SKAO Science Working Group \textit{Our Galaxy}.

AI.tldr: SKAO will revolutionize Galactic astrophysics via wide-field, high-sensitivity, high-resolution spectroscopy and precise astrometry to study matter cycling from star birth to stellar death.
AI.motivation: Understanding matter cycling through the Galaxy (star formation to stellar ejection) requires multi-faceted radio observations.
AI.method: Using the Square Kilometre Array (SKAO) for wide-field, high-sensitivity, high-resolution spectroscopy and precise astrometry.
AI.result: SKAO offers unique capabilities to revolutionize Galactic astrophysics and serve as a model for extragalactic studies.
AI.conclusion: The SKAO will provide transformative insights into Galactic matter cycling, as detailed in chapters from the SKAO Science Working Group "Our Galaxy."

title: Discovery of an Unbound Flyby Companion of UBC 63: In the Immediate Aftermath of a Close Encounter
comment: 10 pages, 11 figures, 2 tables; Accepted for publication in The Astronomical Journal
summary: We re-investigate the open cluster UBC 63 using the Gaia DR3 data and show that, rather than being a single cluster as previously classified, it is a compelling candidate for a double cluster undergoing an unbound flyby interaction. A GMM decomposition performed in the 5D astrometric space reveals the two statistically distinct components, namely UBC 63A (98 members, Age = 21 $\pm$ 4 Myr) and UBC 63B (148 members, Age = 562 $\pm$ 43 Myr). A significant age difference of $Δ\mathrm{Age} = 541 \pm 43$ Myr between the clusters, rules out coeval formation. Their 3D separation of $60 \pm 29$ pc at the birth-epoch of the younger cluster, indicates that the clusters might have originated from the same molecular cloud complex. At present, the system exhibits a 3D separation of $26 \pm 8$ pc, with a relative velocity of $3.60 \pm 1.80$ km s$^{-1}$. Orbital integrations and \textit{N}-body simulations of the pair suggest that the systems had a close encounter, reaching a separation of $7 \pm 2$ pc only $\sim$~6 Myr ago and predict a rapid divergence to a separation of $491 \pm 213$ pc within the next $\sim$100 Myr. The low escape velocity ($V_{\rm esc} = 0.51 \pm 0.12$ km s$^{-1}$) of the system compared to the relative 3D velocity indicates that they are gravitationally unbound. Their low tidal factors, elongated structures and populations extending beyond the Jacobi radii may reflect a strong transient tidal interaction between the clusters.

AI.tldr: UBC 63 is reclassified from a single open cluster to a candidate double cluster (UBC 63A and UBC 63B) undergoing an unbound flyby interaction, revealed by Gaia DR3 data, GMM decomposition, orbital integrations, and N-body simulations.
AI.motivation: To re-investigate the open cluster UBC 63 using Gaia DR3 data, as previous classifications may have missed its true binary nature.
AI.method: Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) decomposition in 5D astrometric space; orbital integrations and N-body simulations of the pair.
AI.result: Two statistically distinct components identified: UBC 63A (98 members, age 21±4 Myr) and UBC 63B (148 members, age 562±43 Myr). Present 3D separation: 26±8 pc; relative velocity: 3.60±1.80 km/s; closest approach 7±2 pc ~6 Myr ago; escape velocity 0.51±0.12 km/s indicates unbound system.
AI.conclusion: UBC 63 is a compelling candidate for a double cluster undergoing an unbound flyby interaction, with significant age difference ruling out coeval formation, but possible common origin in the same molecular cloud complex.
